# Where Bun's WebCore differs from upstream

`README.md` in this directory says what this list is for. Add a line when you change an imported file beyond deleting what Bun does not have.

## The revision

`src/jsc/bindings/webcore/` and `generated/` were made from `Source/WebCore` of oven-sh/WebKit at `b1e30d08cb1428688c5f24109fe4f534096ee2ad`, which has upstream WebKit up to `23b0720b40`. Use that revision to regenerate. After an update from a newer WebKit, change this paragraph.

## Generated files

The scripts are the list. Each entry has a comment that says why.

| What                                                                                                     | Where                                                                                                 |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Members, setters, DOMJIT records and enumerations that are left out                                      | `removedMembers`, `readonlyAttributes`, `withoutDOMJIT`, `removedEnumerations` in `bindings-rules.ts` |
| `[EnabledBySetting]`, `[EnabledForWorld]`, `[SecureContext]`, quirks: decided when the code is generated | `settings`, `otherConditions` in `bindings-rules.ts`                                                  |
| Interfaces that are not `[ActiveDOMObject]`                                                              | `notActiveDOMObjects` in `bindings-rules.ts`                                                          |
| Textual rules for all files and for single files                                                         | `rulesForEveryFile`, `rulesForOneFile` in `bindings-rules.ts`                                         |
| Edited IDL files                                                                                         | `idl/`                                                                                                |
| Partial interfaces that are left out                                                                     | `excluded` in `upstream.ts`                                                                           |
| Lines of `html/HTMLTagNames.in`                                                                          | `tagLines` in `names.ts`                                                                              |
| The SVG tags that have a class. The two SVG factories see only those                                     | `svgTagsWithInterface` in `names.ts`                                                                  |
| Static names that hold a `NodeName` and no strings, and per-VM tables of the `QualifiedName`s            | `makeNamesStatic()` in `names.ts`, `dom/StaticNames.cpp`                                              |
| 16-bit names go through the 8-bit lookup                                                                 | `narrowWideNames()` in `names.ts`                                                                     |

### Code that the generator repeats and Bun shares

The generator prints the same work into every accessor and every class. In Bun that work is in function templates and out-of-line functions, and the generated code calls them. What script sees is the same. The functions in `bindings.ts` do the rewriting.

| What                                                                                                                                                                | Function in `bindings.ts`                | Where the work is now                                                                     |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Accessors of the event handler attributes (`onclick`)                                                                                                               | `outlineEventHandlers()`                 | `bindings/js/JSEventHandlerAttribute.h`, `JSWindowEventHandlerAttribute.h`                |
| Accessors of attributes that reflect a content attribute. `Element.id` and `Element.className` keep the generator's accessors, which are five instructions shorter. | `outlineReflectedAttributes()`           | `bindings/js/JSReflectedAttribute.h`                                                      |
| Structures, prototypes, constructors, the `constructor` getter                                                                                                      | `outlineClassSetup()`                    | `bindings/js/JSDOMClassSetup.{h,cpp}`, `JSDOMConstructorBase::initializeBaseProperties()` |
| `analyzeHeap()` of a class whose base class is a wrapper too: removed, the base class says the same                                                                 | `outlineClassSetup()`                    |                                                                                           |
| The inherited members of a dictionary are converted by the parent dictionary's function                                                                             | `convertInheritedMembersThroughParent()` |                                                                                           |

## Imported files

One section for each upstream directory. A file name is relative to its section's directory. Each section begins with what is cut there as a whole. The list has only what an update from upstream would undo without anybody noticing: one line for each difference, with the reason after _Why:_.

### dom/

Bun's DOM is a tree with events: nothing is rendered, loaded, navigated or run. Gone, with their members, parameters, files and `#include` lines, are frames, pages, renderers, layout, style resolution and invalidation, the loader, the decoder, libxml2, `Settings`, `Quirks`, security origins, content security policy, the inspector, accessibility, editing, media, fullscreen, platform events, pseudo-elements, mutation events, isolated worlds and IPC. Some files that upstream has in `dom/` sit directly in `webcore/` in Bun (`EventTarget.*`, `Event.*`, `EventPath.*`, `EventContext.*`, `EventListenerMap.*`, `RegisteredEventListener.*`, `AddEventListenerOptions.h`, `EventNames.*`, the lists of events and event targets, `ActiveDOMObject.*`, `ContextDestructionObserver.*` and others), and `ActiveDOMCallback.*` and `ExceptionCode.h` are in `src/jsc/bindings/`.

- (all files): State that holds nodes, `AtomString`s, `QualifiedName`s or counters has to be a member of `DOMClientData`. Upstream keeps it in a `static NeverDestroyed`, a `MainThreadNeverDestroyed`, a file-level static or `ThreadGlobalData`. _Why:_ Bun has a VM per thread, and each can have its own DOM. An `AtomString` belongs to one thread.
- (all files): A pointer such as `&classAttr.get()` must not be kept in a `static`, because it points into one VM's table. Keep the `StaticQualifiedName` or its address. A function that takes a `const HTMLQualifiedName&` says `name.get().localName()` or compares `nodeName()`. _Why:_ `HTMLQualifiedName` derives from `StaticQualifiedName`, not from `QualifiedName`.
- (all files): Each test of a setting is decided in the source, with upstream's default for WebCore. The exceptions: `MathMLEnabled` counts as false, and `ScopedCustomElementRegistryEnabled` is false although Safari has it on. The values have to agree with `settings` in `bindings-rules.ts`. _Why:_ Nothing can change a setting at run time. `mathml/` is not imported.
- (all files): `MutationEventsEnabled` and `ShadowRootReferenceTargetEnabled` are false, and the code behind them is deleted in every file. `Element::resolveReferenceTarget()` returns the element and `retargetReferenceTargetForBindings()` returns its argument. _Why:_ Both are upstream's defaults. The two functions stay because `TreeScope.cpp`, `CustomElementDefaultARIA.cpp` and `html/` call them.
- (all files): Blocks under `ENABLE(FULLSCREEN_API)`, `ENABLE(VIDEO)` and `ENABLE(MATHML)` are deleted, although all three are 1 in Bun's `cmakeconfig.h`. `PLATFORM(COCOA)` is never defined, on macOS too, so only the other branch is kept. _Why:_ The parts behind the flags are cut. New upstream text under them would be compiled, so it has to be deleted again.
- (all files): For new upstream text that calls a cut member of `Document`: an accessor that returns a pointer (`page()`, `frame()`, `view()`, `renderView()`, `loader()`, `existingAXObjectCache()`, every `...IfExists()`) takes the null branch, and `quirks().x()` is false. `isTopDocument()`, `haveStylesheetsLoaded()`, `allowsContentJavaScript()`, `shouldNotFireMutationEvents()` and `securityOrigin()` checks are true, `shouldMaskURLForBindings()` is false, and `mainFrameDocument()` is the document itself. Calls that update or schedule style, layout or rendering, and `addConsoleMessage()`, are deleted. _Why:_ One rule for all imported files. The lines about `m_window` and `setFocusedElement()` are the exceptions.
- (all files): `Window` stands in for `LocalDOMWindow`, `DOMWindow` and `WindowProxy`. Every `RefPtr<WindowProxy>` of the UI event classes is a `RefPtr<Window>`, `view()` returns `Window*`, and `windowProxy()` becomes `window()`. The headers only forward-declare `Window`, so a `.cpp` that declares an init dictionary of these classes includes `Window.h`. _Why:_ There is no `WindowProxy`: a `Window` is an ordinary wrapped object.
- `AbstractRange.h`, `CustomElementRegistry.h`, `DOMRectList.h`, `MutationObserver.h`, `MutationRecord.h`: Each class also derives from `ScriptWrappable`. The same holds for `DOMTokenList` and `ValidityState` in `html/`. _Why:_ Bun has no map of wrappers per world. A class that is not `ScriptWrappable` gets a new wrapper on every `toJS()`, and nothing keeps that wrapper alive.
- `ActiveDOMCallback.cpp`: `canInvokeCallback()` is `context && !context->isStopped() && !context->isJSExecutionForbidden()`. _Why:_ Bun's loop keeps draining its queue for the rest of the tick after the VM's stop is requested. `isStopped()` covers the context of a disposed module graph.
- `ActiveDOMObject.{h,cpp}`: Bun's own trimmed copy: do not copy upstream's text over it. The pending activity count is atomic. _Why:_ GC threads read the count. No class in `dom/` or `html/` derives from it.
- `AddEventListenerOptions.h`, `RegisteredEventListener.h`, `EventTarget.cpp`: The last option is `resistStopPropagation`, where upstream has `webkitTrustedOnly` and `trustedOnly`. After `stopImmediatePropagation()` the loop goes on and runs only the listeners that resist. _Why:_ It mirrors Node.js's `kResistStopPropagation`, which Bun's internal modules set through a private symbol.
- `CharacterData.cpp`, `Document.cpp`, `Element.cpp`: Three differences have no reason any more, so upstream's text can come back. `canUseSetDataOptimization()` lacks the test for a `<style>` parent, the `nonce` case of `attributeChanged()` tests `is<HTMLElement>` and not `SVGElement`, and `bodyOrFrameset()` and `setBodyOrFrameset()` compare tag names. _Why:_ Bun has style sheets, `SVGElement` and `HTMLFrameSetElement`.
- `ChildListMutationScope.{h,cpp}`, `ContainerNodeAlgorithms.{h,cpp}`, `GCReachableRef.{h,cpp}`, `QualifiedName.cpp`, `ScopedEventQueue.{h,cpp}`, `SimulatedClick.cpp`: These come from `domClientData()`: the accumulator map, the current `ContainerChildRemovalScope` (debug builds only), `GCReachableRefMap::map()`, the name cache, `ScopedEventQueue::singleton()` and the set of elements that are dispatching a simulated click. _Why:_ Upstream has them in `ThreadGlobalData` or in statics.
- `ContainerNode.cpp`: `insertBefore()`, `replaceChild()` and the two `...WithoutPreInsertionValidityCheck()` functions do not validate again after the new child has left its old parent. The `scriptExecutionCount()` blocks and `checkAcceptChildGuaranteedNodeTypes()` are gone, and `removeAllChildrenWithScriptAssertion()` does not collect the children a second time. _Why:_ Only mutation events and `unload` of a subframe could run script there. If anything ever runs script synchronously under `removeChild()`, the blocks have to come back.
- `ContextDestructionObserver.cpp`: `observeContext()` uses the raw pointer, where upstream makes a `RefPtr`. _Why:_ An observer that dies inside `~ScriptExecutionContext` would ref a context that is being destroyed.
- `CustomElementReactionQueue.{h,cpp}`, `Document.{h,cpp}`: The processing stack and the debug counter of `CustomElementReactionDisallowedScope` are per VM. A `CustomElementReactionStack` looks its slot up once, in its constructor, so its `JSGlobalObject*` must not be null. The backup queue is `Document::backupElementQueue()`, and its microtask holds a `Ref` to the document. _Why:_ Upstream has two statics, and the queue is in `WindowEventLoop`, one per agent.
- `Document.cpp`: `explicitClose()` always takes upstream's path for a document without a frame: `readyState` becomes `complete` and `implicitClose()` runs at once. `implicitClose()` has three steps: detach the parser, `Window::scrollToFragment()` (which only sets the `:target` element), the `load` event. _Why:_ Nothing is loaded, so parsing is synchronous.
- `Document.cpp`: `finishedParsing()` is `setParsing(false)`, `DOMContentLoaded` and dropping the shared object pool. There is no microtask checkpoint, and the pool is not kept for 10 more seconds. _Why:_ Parsing always runs under script, where the standard forbids a checkpoint. `Document` has no `Timer`.
- `Document.cpp`: `lastModified()` is the current local time, read with `PlainGregorianDateTime::currentLocalTime()` instead of `std::localtime()`. _Why:_ `std::localtime()` returns one static buffer for all threads.
- `Document.cpp`: `setMarkupUnsafe()` sets quirks mode before it tries the fast path parser. `open()` resets the mode on the slow path. _Why:_ The fast path gives up at a doctype, so what it parses is in quirks mode. Upstream leaves such a document in no-quirks mode.
- `Document.cpp`, `DOMImplementation.cpp`, `XMLDocument.{h,cpp}`: `createElement(const QualifiedName&, ...)` makes an `SVGElement` for every name in the SVG namespace and a plain `Element` for MathML. The new `XMLDocument::createSVG()` stands in for `SVGDocument::create()`. _Why:_ `svg/` has one class, and `mathml/` is not imported.
- `Document.cpp`, `MutationRecord.cpp`, `PointerEventTypeNames.{h,cpp}`, `ShadowRootMode.h`, `SlotAssignmentMode.h`: Function-local static `AtomString`s become common atoms (`childListAtom()`, `openAtom()`, `namedAtom()`) or a literal (`"color-profile"_s` in `isStandardElementName()`). `mousePointerEventType()` returns a `String` by value, made with `MAKE_STATIC_STRING_IMPL`. _Why:_ An `AtomString` belongs to one thread. A static `StringImpl` may be shared.
- `Document.h`: `incDOMTreeVersion()` increments a counter of the document. Upstream has the process-wide `s_globalTreeVersion`. _Why:_ With a VM per thread the shared counter is an unsynchronized write. All readers compare two versions of one document.
- `Document.h`: `m_documentElementTextDirection` is initialized to `TextDirection::LTR`. _Why:_ Upstream leaves it uninitialized until the first document element.
- `Document.{h,cpp}`: `window()` returns the raw back pointer `Window* m_window`, which the new `setWindow()` sets. The constructor sets the "uses the null custom element registry" flag. `setWindow()` clears it and takes the window's registry, so it has to run before anything is created in or parsed into the document. _Why:_ `Window` stands in for `LocalDOMWindow`, and the window owns the document.
- `Document.{h,cpp}`: Tests for a frame or a page become tests for `m_window` in `hasBrowsingContext()`, `isFullyActive()`, `hasFocus()`, `visibilityState()`, `isCookieAverse()`, `setReadyState()` (the `readystatechange` dispatch) and `open()` (the parser test). _Why:_ No frames or pages. A document that has a window counts as active, focused and visible.
- `Document.{h,cpp}`: `ownerElement()` is `Window::frameElement()` and returns an `Element*`, `parentDocument()` is that element's document, and `isSrcdocDocument()` tests the URL. `fallbackBaseURL()` has upstream's text on top of them. `dispatchWindowLoadEvent()` also fires `load` at the owner element, which `LocalDOMWindow::dispatchLoadEvent()` does upstream. `referrerForBindings()` is the parent document's URL. _Why:_ A frame is only a `Window` that a frame element owns. See `html/HTMLFrameElementBase`.
- `Document.{h,cpp}`: `cookie()` and `setCookie()` work on an in-memory jar, `Vector<Ref<Cookie>> m_cookies`. Bun's own `Cookie::parse()` reads the string. _Why:_ There is no network process to ask.
- `Document.{h,cpp}`: `parseHTMLUnsafe()` takes `String&&`. `write()` and `writeln()` take `FixedVector<String>&&`. _Why:_ No trusted types.
- `Document.{h,cpp}`, `Element.cpp`: `setFocusedElement()` always dispatches blur and focus, where upstream first asks the page's focus controller. `Element::focus()` and `blur()` call it instead of `FocusController::setFocusedElement()`. An element that takes the focus in a frame's document takes it from the documents above and below, and `TreeScope::focusedElementInScope()` gives those the frame from `Document::focusedFrameOwnerElement()`, where upstream asks the controller for the focused frame. _Why:_ `FocusController` belongs to `Page`.
- `Document.{h,cpp}`, `Node.cpp`: `Document` derives from `ContainerNode` and `TreeScope` only: it is not a `ScriptExecutionContext`. It holds `const Ref<ScriptExecutionContext> m_scriptExecutionContext`, which `create()` takes and `Node::scriptExecutionContext()` returns. `contextDocument()` is gone: template documents, clones, `new Document()`, `createHTMLDocument()` and `parseHTMLUnsafe()` copy the `Ref`. Where upstream passes a `Document&` as a context, Bun passes `*document.scriptExecutionContext()`. _Why:_ Bun has its own `ScriptExecutionContext`, one per global object or `ModuleGraph`.
- `DocumentEventLoop.cpp`, `Document.h`: New, in place of `EventLoop.cpp` and `WindowEventLoop.cpp`: `eventLoop()` and `postTask()` become `Document::queueTask()`, `queueMicrotask()` and `performMicrotaskCheckpoint()`. `queueTask()` posts to the context, ignores the `TaskSource` and captures a `Window::PendingTask`. After 1,000 tasks in one turn of the loop it uses `postTaskAfterYield()`, and the count is per VM. _Why:_ Bun has one event loop per VM. `postTask()` also runs what is queued while it drains, so tasks that queue tasks would starve timers and I/O.
- `DOMClientData.{h,cpp}`: New: the DOM's per-VM state. `willDestroyVM()` empties what holds nodes, then what holds names, then the name cache, then the thread's slot, and a new member that holds nodes or names has to be added there. `domClientData()` without an argument reads `Thread::currentSingleton().m_clientData`, the slot that upstream uses for `ThreadGlobalData`. _Why:_ The last reference to a name removes it from the name cache, so the cache has to outlive the rest. The slot needs no new `thread_local`.
- `DOMPoint.*`, `DOMPointReadOnly.*`, `DOMPointInit.h`: Not in Bun. _Why:_ The interfaces are undefined: see Behavior.
- `DragEvent.{h,cpp}`, `ClipboardEvent.{h,cpp}`: `dataTransfer()` and `clipboardData()` return a `const JSValueInWrappedObject&`, and the init members are `JSC::JSValue`. The native `create()` functions that take a `DataTransfer` are gone. _Why:_ `DataTransfer` is not imported: it needs `Pasteboard`, `DragImage`, `CachedImage` and more.
- `TouchEvent.{h,cpp}`: It derives from `UIEventWithKeyState`, where upstream has `MouseRelatedEvent`, and is not under `ENABLE(TOUCH_EVENTS)`. The three lists are `JSValueInWrappedObject`s that hold JavaScript arrays. `create()` copies whatever can be iterated into new arrays and hands them to the caller in a `MarkedArgumentBuffer`: the generated constructor holds them until the wrapper exists (`rulesForOneFile`). The getters are in `bindings/js/JSTouchEventCustom.cpp` and make an empty array for a list that nobody gave. `Touch.*` is not imported, and `TouchList.h` and the touch code of `EventContext` and `EventPath` stay under the flag, which is off. _Why:_ jsdom has no `Touch` and no `TouchList`, and tests pass plain objects. Nothing native makes touch events, so nothing retargets them.
- `Element.cpp`: `isFocusable()` is `isConnected() && supportsFocus() && !isInert(*this)`. The new static `isInert()` walks up the composed tree: an HTML ancestor with `inert` means inert, the active modal dialog reached first means not inert, and an open modal dialog that is not reached means inert. _Why:_ Upstream reads `effectiveInert`, an inherited style bit that `Style::Adjuster` sets by the same three rules. The walk costs the depth of the tree for each call.
- `Element.cpp`: `supportsFocus()` is also true for an SVG `<a>` with `href` or `xlink:href`, and `defaultTabIndex()` is 0 for an SVG `<a>`. _Why:_ Upstream says both in `SVGAElement`, which is not imported. user-event's `tab()` calls `focus()` on each `a[href]` and never gets past one that refuses.
- `Element.cpp`: Both `removeAttribute()` overloads call `synchronizeAttribute()` first. Upstream's special case for a dirty `style` attribute, with `removeAllInlineStyleProperties()`, is gone. _Why:_ The attribute is written back and then removed like any other, so there is a mutation record and no `style=""` is left.
- `Element.{h,cpp}`: `setInnerHTML()`, `setOuterHTML()`, `setHTMLUnsafe()` and `insertAdjacentHTML(where, markup)` take `String&&` instead of `Variant<Ref<TrustedHTML>, String>&&`, and do not begin with `trustedTypeCompliantString()`. The `setAttribute()` and `setAttributeNS()` overloads that take a `TrustedTypeOrString` are gone: their bodies are the `const AtomString&` overloads. _Why:_ Bun has no trusted types. Nothing could make one, because there is no policy factory.
- `Element.{h,cpp}`, `ElementInlines.h`, `ElementData.h`: New overloads take a `StaticQualifiedName` by value: `hasTagName`, `hasAttribute`, `getAttribute`, `hasAttributeWithoutSynchronization`, `attributeWithoutSynchronization`, `findAttributeByName`, `findAttributeIndexByName`, `getAttributeInternal`, `synchronizeAttribute`, `fastAttributeLookupAllowed`. The bodies are copies of the `const QualifiedName&` ones, so change both together. _Why:_ The hot lookups compare enumerators and never touch the per-VM table. Every other function gets a static name through the conversion, which is one table lookup.
- `Element.{h,cpp}`, `ElementRareData.h`, `CustomElementRegistry.{h,cpp}`: An element's list of `Attr` nodes and its scoped registry are members of `ElementRareData` (`Vector<Ref<Attr>>`, `RefPtr<CustomElementRegistry>`). The functions around upstream's maps keep their names: `attrNodeListForElement()`, `addToScopedCustomElementRegistryMap()`, `registryForElement()` and the like. _Why:_ Upstream has two process-wide maps.
- `Event.cpp`: `timeStampForBindings()` takes the `Performance` of the context's global object and calls `relativeTimeFromTimeOrigin()`. Upstream takes the window's or the worker's and calls `relativeTimeFromTimeOriginInReducedResolution()`. _Why:_ The context is neither a `Document` nor a `WorkerGlobalScope`. Bun's `performance.now()` is not coarsened either.
- `EventContext.{h,cpp}`: `m_contextNodeIsFormElement` is gone, and with it the block of `handleLocalEvents()` that stops a `submit` or `reset` event from a descendant at the form. The constructor that takes a `Node&` is in the `.cpp` file, and the header does not include `HTMLFormElement.h`. _Why:_ See "`submit` and `reset` from inside a form" under Forms. Bun's event dispatch also serves `EventTarget`s that are not nodes, and does not need the forms headers.
- `EventInterfaces.h`, `EventHeaders.h`, `EventFactory.cpp`, `EventTargetInterfaces.h`, `EventTargetHeaders.h`, `EventTargetFactory.cpp`: Kept by hand, where upstream makes them with `make_event_factory.pl`. They list only the classes Bun has, plus `BunWebView`, and a new event target class needs a number here. `DOMWindow` is what Bun's `GlobalEventScope` returns, and the factory turns it into the global object. The DOM's window is `Window`. _Why:_ The generated lists name about 200 classes that Bun lacks. The global object's own listeners are older than the DOM.
- `EventListenerMap.{h,cpp}`, `RegisteredEventListener.{h,cpp}`, `EventTarget.{h,cpp}`: `EventListenerMap::add()` returns a `RegisteredEventListener*` instead of a `bool`. The listener remembers its `AbortSignal` and the id of its abort algorithm, and `markAsRemoved()` removes the algorithm. `EventTargetData::clear()` calls `eventListenerMap.clear()` instead of `clearEntriesForTearDown()`, so the same happens when the target dies. _Why:_ A long-lived signal that is used for many listeners does not collect dead algorithms.
- `EventNames.{h,cpp}`: `eventNames()` is only declared in the header, and the `.cpp` ends with a `thread_local` holder, `eventNames()` and `Bun__domEventNameToJS()`. `handshakeEvent` and `renameEvent` follow `zoomEvent`. They are not in `EventType`, so `typeInfoForEvent()` does not know them. _Why:_ `ThreadGlobalData` is not imported. Bun's native code asks for event names, and the two events belong to Bun's own classes.
- `EventNames.{h,cpp}`: `m_typeInfoMap` is filled by a loop over a constant table, and `EventTypeInfo`'s constructors are `constexpr`. The constructor and an out-of-line destructor have `__attribute__((minsize))`. _Why:_ 340 members made and destroyed in straight-line code were 63 KB.
- `EventTarget.cpp`: The static `shouldMakeEventListenerPassive()` stands in for `Quirks::shouldMakeEventListenerPassive()`. It has upstream's logic with both "passive by default" settings taken as true: touch and wheel events on the window, the document, `<html>` and `<body>`. _Why:_ `Quirks` is cut, but this part of it is the standard's "default passive value".
- `EventTarget.cpp`: For an event that is being dispatched, `dispatchEventForBindings()` returns `InvalidStateError` only when the target is a `Node`. Other targets get Node.js's `EVENT_RECURSION` error. _Why:_ One `EventTarget` serves Node.js semantics and the DOM.
- `EventTarget.cpp`: `fireEventListeners()` returns when `scriptExecutionContext()` is null. _Why:_ The context of a `ModuleGraph` can be collected while the host still holds the target.
- `EventTarget.h`: `WeakPtrImplWithEventTargetData` derives from `WeakPtrImplBaseSingleThread` instead of `WeakPtrImplBase`. A `WeakPtr<Node>` may not be copied or dropped on another thread. _Why:_ The count is not atomic, which is cheaper.
- `EventTarget.{h,cpp}`, `EventTargetInlines.h`: `EventTargetData` has the flag `isFiringEventListeners`, which `fireEventListeners()` sets with `SetForScope`. `EventTarget::isFiringEventListeners()` reads it. _Why:_ The wrappers of `AbortSignal` and `WebSocket` stay alive while it is set. Upstream dropped it.
- `ExceptionCode.h`: The enumeration is unscoped and has five more codes: `InvalidThisError`, `InvalidURLError`, `CryptoOperationFailedError`, `EVENT_RECURSION`, `WORKER_INVALID_EXEC_ARGV`. `DOMExceptionCode` in `src/jsc/JSErrorCode.rs` has to stay in sync. _Why:_ Node.js's errors.
- `ExceptionCode.h` (its users): `ExceptionCode::SyntaxError` means a `DOMException`, as upstream. In `src/jsc/bindings/`, `webcore/WebSocket.cpp`, `webcore/PerformanceUserTiming.cpp`, `webcrypto/*` and `node/crypto/KeyObject.cpp` say `JSSyntaxError` where upstream says `SyntaxError`. _Why:_ Released code depends on `instanceof SyntaxError` for those APIs.
- `InlineStyleSheetOwner.{h,cpp}`: Lazy: a change of the text drops the sheet and sets `m_sheetNeedsUpdate`, and `sheet(Element&)` parses. `setContentType()` and `setMedia()` take the element. _Why:_ Libraries such as emotion append hundreds of `<style>` elements that nobody may ever ask about.
- `MessageEvent.{h,cpp}`, `JSMessageEvent.cpp`: `source` is a `RefPtr<EventTarget>` (a `MessagePort` or a `Window`) in the member, `Init`, the accessor, `create()` and `initMessageEvent()`. Upstream has `Variant<Ref<WindowProxy>, Ref<MessagePort>, Ref<ServiceWorker>>`. The dictionary converts a window through `JSWindow::toWrapped()`. Any other object is `Init::sourceObject` and `m_jsSource`, a `JSValueInWrappedObject` that the wrapper visits, and `acceptsAnyObjectAsSource()` in the binding says when one is taken. _Why:_ There is no `WindowProxy` and no `ServiceWorker`.
- `MutationObserver.{h,cpp}`: The active observers, the signal slot list, two flags and the counter that orders deliveries are in the new `struct MutationObserverAgentData`, one per VM. `queueCompoundMicrotask(Document&)` stands in for `WindowEventLoop::queueMutationObserverCompoundMicrotask()` and uses `Document::queueMicrotask()`. There is no list of suspended observers: an observer whose callback cannot be invoked is skipped and keeps its records. _Why:_ Upstream has them in `WindowEventLoop` and in the static `s_observerPriority`. If `queueMicrotask()` ever drops a callback, `compoundMicrotaskQueued` stays set and no observer of the VM is notified again.
- `Node.h`: `StateFlag` and `TypeFlag` lose the enumerators of the cut parts. The ones that stay keep upstream's bit values. _Why:_ With the same values the next merge only deletes lines.
- `Node.{h,cpp}`: `computeEditability()` takes no arguments and returns `HTMLElement::editabilityFromContentEditableAttr(*this)`. _Why:_ Editability does not look at style (`-webkit-user-modify`, `user-select`).
- `Node.{h,cpp}`, `NodeInlines.h`, `Document.cpp`, `Attr.h`, `Range.h`, `TreeWalker.h`: The main thread assertions are gone. `WTF_DECLARE_OWNER_THREAD_ASSERTIONS(lock, mainThreadLike)` says `anyThreadLike`, which keeps the lock annotations and lets the run-time check pass. _Why:_ The DOM works on every thread that has a VM.
- `QualifiedName.h`: `operator==(const QualifiedName&, StaticQualifiedName)` is `a.nodeName() == b.nodeName() && !a.hasPrefix()`, and `matches(StaticQualifiedName)` is `nodeName() == other.nodeName()`. _Why:_ No table lookup. The meaning is upstream's as long as no static name has a prefix, none is `NodeName::Unknown`, and `m_nodeName` depends only on the namespace and the local name.
- `QualifiedName.{h,cpp}`, `StaticNames.{h,cpp}`: `StaticQualifiedName` and `StaticNamespaceURI` are new: each is `constexpr` and holds only a `NodeName` or a `Namespace` enumerator. `get()`, an implicit conversion and `->` give the VM's `QualifiedName` or `AtomString`, so call sites keep upstream's spelling. The new `StaticNames` holds one VM's tables, each entry filled on first use. `anyName`, `nullName` and `QualifiedName::init()` are gone: `anyQName()` and `nullQName()` return the VM's copy. _Why:_ Upstream's `HTMLNames::divTag` is a process-wide `QualifiedName`, which holds `AtomString`s. The tables replace about 1,000 globals and their `init()` functions.
- `Range.{h,cpp}`: `createContextualFragment()` takes `String&&`. _Why:_ No trusted types.
- `ScriptDisallowedScope.h`, `ContainerNode.cpp`: The count and the current `EventAllowedScope` are per VM and exist only with `ASSERT_ENABLED`. In a release build the scopes are empty and `isScriptAllowed()` is true. The `isMainThread()` and `isInWebProcess()` escapes and `DisableAssertionsInScope` are gone, so in a debug build the assertions are real on every thread. _Why:_ Upstream counts in the process-wide `s_count`, which only assertions read. `isInWebProcess()` is always false in Bun, so upstream's checks would never fire.
- `ScriptableDocumentParser.h`: `wellFormed()` is declared here. _Why:_ Upstream declares it in `DecodedDataDocumentParser`, which is not in Bun.
- `ScriptElement.cpp`: The table `supportedJavaScriptMIMETypes` is copied from `platform/MIMETypeRegistry.cpp` and has to be kept in sync. _Why:_ Of `MIMETypeRegistry` only `isXMLMIMEType()` is imported.
- `ScriptElement.cpp`: `isScriptElement(Node&)` is true for `HTMLScriptElement` and for any element named `script` in the SVG namespace. `dynamicDowncastScriptElement()` only knows `HTMLScriptElement`. _Why:_ `SVGScriptElement` is not imported. A parse without `AllowScriptingContent` still has to drop SVG scripts.
- `ScriptElement.{h,cpp}`: `prepareScript()` keeps upstream's signature, stops after "set already started to true" and always returns false. `ScriptElement` is not an `ActiveDOMObject`. _Why:_ That is where upstream stops in a document without a frame. The parser still calls it.
- `SelectorQuery.cpp`: `SelectorQueryCache::add()` calls `parseCSSSelectorList(selectors, inQuirksMode)` from `css/parser/BunSelectorParser.h`, where upstream uses `CSSTokenizer` and `CSSSelectorParser`. The `resolveNestingParent` step is gone. _Why:_ Rust parses selectors. It emits `&` as `:where(:scope)` itself.
- `SelectorQuery.cpp`: `canOptimizeSingleAttributeExactMatch()` tests `attributeMatchType() != CaseSensitive`. It does not call `HTMLDocument::isCaseSensitiveAttribute()` or `SVGElement::animatableAttributeForName()`. _Why:_ The match type already says how the value is compared. SVG animation is cut.
- `SelectorQuery.{h,cpp}`: There are no `Compilable*` and `Compiled*` match types. `closest()`, `executeSingleSelectorData()` and `executeSingleMultiSelectorData()` build the `SelectorChecker` and the `CheckingContext` once per call, not once per element. _Why:_ There is no selector JIT (`cssjit/` is not in Bun), and upstream leaves that speed to it.
- `SelectorQuery.{h,cpp}`, `Document.cpp`: `SelectorQueryCache::singleton()` is gone: the cache is `domClientData(vm()).selectorQueryCache()`. The key is the selector `String`, in one of two maps, `m_entries` and `m_quirksModeEntries`. Upstream's key is `(String, CSSSelectorParserContext, SecurityOriginData)`. _Why:_ The cache holds `QualifiedName`s and `AtomString`s. The document's mode is the only input besides the text that changes the result.
- `ShadowRoot.{h,cpp}`: `setInnerHTML()` and `setHTMLUnsafe()` take `String&&`. _Why:_ No trusted types.
- `SpaceSplitString.{h,cpp}`: The table of shared class lists is `domClientData().spaceSplitStrings()`, one per VM, instead of a process-wide `static NeverDestroyed` map. The `ASSERT(isMainThread())` lines are gone. _Why:_ With upstream's text, two threads that set `class` attributes at the same time corrupt the map and crash.
- `StyledElement.{h,cpp}`: `inlineStyle()` is out of line and parses the `style` attribute on first use. `styleAttributeChanged()` drops `m_inlineStyle`, or parses into the same object if script holds `element.style`. Upstream parses when the attribute changes. _Why:_ Markup with `style="..."` that nobody reads costs nothing.
- `StyledElement.cpp`: `dirtyStyleAttribute()` adds an empty `style` attribute if the element has none, and `invalidateStyleAttribute()` calls it. _Why:_ Upstream adds the attribute when somebody reads it, so it stands after attributes that were set later. The standard and jsdom put it where it was first written, and snapshots of markup show the order.
- `TrustedHTML.*`, `TrustedScript.*`, `TrustedScriptURL.*`, `TrustedType.*`: Not in Bun. _Why:_ No trusted types.
- `Window.{h,cpp}`: New, in place of `page/DOMWindow`, `LocalDOMWindow`, `RemoteDOMWindow` and `WindowProxy`. A `Window` is a `RefCounted` `EventTarget` made by `Window::create(ScriptExecutionContext&, Options&&)`, and it owns its document. What needs a screen or a user maps to `doNothing()`. _Why:_ A window is an ordinary object from `new Window()`, not the global object. The runtime has its own `performance`, `crypto`, `navigator` and timers.
- `Window.{h,cpp}`: The listener overrides call `Document::didAddEventListenersOfType()` and `didRemoveEventListenersOfType()`, as `LocalDOMWindow` does. _Why:_ Without those calls `EventDispatcher` returns early, and a listener on the window never hears an event from a node.
- `Window.{h,cpp}`: `Window::PendingTask` is a move-only token that holds the window and counts in the atomic `m_pendingTaskCount`. While the count is not zero the collector keeps the window's wrapper, and with it the wrappers and listeners of its nodes. `close()` sets the count to 0 for good. _Why:_ Upstream's window is the global object, which nothing has to keep alive. Here a window with a queued `message` or `hashchange` and no other reference would be collected before the event.
- `Window.{h,cpp}`: `Window::CurrentEventScope` and `forEventTarget()` hold `window.event`, which upstream keeps in `JSDOMWindowBase`. `reportException()` is the standard's "report an exception" for one window: it fires `error` at the window and then calls `window.console.error`, looked up as script would. _Why:_ A realm has many windows, so the window comes from the event's current target. React 16 to 18 in development mode pick exceptions up from the window's `error` event, and a spy on `console.error` sees or silences the rest.
- `Window.{h,cpp}`: `loadingRequests()` is a weak set of the window's `XMLHttpRequest`s that are loading, which `XMLHttpRequestLoader` keeps. `close()` calls `stop()` on each. `forEventTarget()` also knows a request and its upload. _Why:_ Upstream's document is the context and stops its active objects. Here they belong to the global object's context, which lives on.
- `Window.{h,cpp}`: A window also does what is left of `Frame` and `FrameTree`. `createForFrame()` makes the window in a frame, `m_frameElement` points back at the frame element weakly, and `parent()`, `top()`, `length()`, `item()` and `namedItem()` are worked out from the frame elements of the document, in tree order. `m_frameElements` and `m_openedWindows` are weak sets that `close()` goes through. `open()` makes a window with `m_opener`. `finishLoadingFrameSoon()` collects the frames' windows that have yet to hear `load` and queues one microtask for all of them, and a frame that goes takes its window out of the list. `close(CanRunScript::No)` is for a frame element that is being removed: it stops the `XMLHttpRequest`s in a task. _Why:_ Nothing is loaded, so a frame needs no loader, history or view. Cancelling a request runs script, which `removingSteps()` and a destructor must not do.
- `Window.{h,cpp}`: `createForFrame()` makes the wrapper at once. `containerOpaqueRoot()` is the document of the frame element as an atomic pointer that is only compared: the wrapper is reachable from that root and adds it, and it adds the root of the opener's document. _Why:_ Upstream's frames hold their windows with `JSC::Strong`. Here a window and the windows of its frames have to live and die together, in both directions. A window without a wrapper in the middle of the chain would break it, and the collector's threads must not follow a pointer to a frame element.
- `Window.{h,cpp}`: `requestAnimationFrame()`, `cancelAnimationFrame()` and `runAnimationFrameCallbacks()` handle the list as `ScriptedAnimationController` does, which is not imported. The frame is one `Bun__Timer__setTimeout`, set by `scheduleAnimationFrame()` in `bindings/js/JSWindowCustom.cpp`, for 1000 / 60 ms after the frame before it, or at once if that is past. Its argument is the window's wrapper. _Why:_ There is no display. A timer keeps the process and the window alive until the frame. It is on the real clock, as in jsdom: `useRealTimers()` drops what waits on the fake one, and a library that took the function before `useFakeTimers()` would get no frame again.

### html/

No file here calls `settings()`, `quirks()`, `renderer()`, `frame()`, `page()`, `AXObjectCache`, `addConsoleMessage()`, `updateLayout()` or style invalidation. The overrides, members and base classes for rendering, presentational hints, loading, navigation, editing, pickers, autofill, state restoration and media are gone, and so are `shadow/` and `forms/`: no form control has a user-agent shadow root. Each test of a setting is replaced by the branch for upstream's `WebCore` default, unless a row says otherwise.

- `Autofill.cpp`, `HTMLAnchorElement.cpp`, `HTMLButtonElement.{h,cpp}`, `HTMLElement.cpp`, `HTMLFieldSetElement.cpp`, `HTMLFormControlElement.{h,cpp}`, `HTMLOutputElement.cpp`, `HTMLTableCellElement.{h,cpp}`, `HTMLTextFormControlElement.{h,cpp}`: Function-local static `AtomString`s are gone. `isContactToken()`, `relList()` and `commandType()` compare with literals, `toValidDirValue()` returns `ltrAtom()` and `rtlAtom()`, and `formControlType()` returns the tag's `localName()`. `scope()` returns `AtomString` by value, and `selectionDirection()`, `popoverTargetAction()` and `command()` return `String`. Command names are compared with `equalIgnoringASCIICase`, because they contain `-`. _Why:_ An `AtomString` belongs to its thread, and the DOM works on every thread. None is a hot path.
- `closewatcher/`, `HTMLDialogElement.{h,cpp}`, `HTMLElement.cpp`: `closewatcher/` is not in Bun. A dialog or a popover makes no close watcher, and `HTMLDialogElement::attributeChanged()` only updates `m_isOpen`. _Why:_ A close request only comes from a trusted key event in `EventHandler`, which Bun does not have.
- `ColorInputType.cpp`: `sanitizeValue()` accepts only `#rrggbb` (new static `isValidSimpleColor()`), lower-cases it, and falls back to `#000000`. _Why:_ Upstream parses any CSS color and serializes it by `alpha` and `colorspace`. That needs `Color` and the CSS parser.
- `CustomElementFormValue.h`, `FormAssociatedCustomElement.{h,cpp}`, `FileInputType.{h,cpp}`: `Ref<Blob>` stands for `Ref<File>`. `appendFormData()` always passes `fileName()`, and an empty file list appends an empty `Blob` with an empty name. _Why:_ Bun's C++ has no `File`: a file is a `Blob` with a name. `DOMFormData::append(name, blob)` without a file name resets the blob's name.
- `DOMFormData.{h,cpp}`: Bun's own class, in `src/jsc/bindings/`. Only `create(ScriptExecutionContext&, HTMLFormElement*, HTMLElement* submitter)` is upstream's text. There is no `TextEncoding` and no `encoding()`, so `HiddenInputType.cpp` appends the literal `"UTF-8"` for `_charset_`. _Why:_ `new FormData(form, submitter)` has to collect the form's entries. Documents are always UTF-8.
- `DOMTokenList.h`: `DOMTokenList` derives from `ScriptWrappable`. _Why:_ Bun has no wrapper map. Without this base, `el.classList === el.classList` is false.
- `EmailInputType.cpp`: `isValidEmailAddress()` is a hand-written scan without state (with `isEmailLocalPartCharacter()`), instead of a `static NeverDestroyed<const JSC::Yarr::RegularExpression>`. _Why:_ `match()` writes to the shared object and allocates from the pattern's own allocator without a lock. Two VMs would race.
- `FormAtomStrings.h`, `InputTypeNames.cpp`, `InputMode.cpp`, `HTMLSelectElement.cpp`: `FormAtomStrings.h` is new: a struct of the 18 atoms that form getters return by reference (14 input type names, `select-one`, `select-multiple`, `numeric`, `decimal`). `DOMClientData` owns one per VM, and a member of `formAtomStrings()` replaces each `static MainThreadNeverDestroyed<const AtomString>`. _Why:_ An `AtomString` belongs to its thread.
- `GenericCachedHTMLCollection.{h,cpp}`: Only `children`, `document.forms`, `document.images` and `document.links` have `CachedHTMLCollection`, its index cache and its traversal for themselves (`hasOwnCachedHTMLCollection()`). The other ten types derive from `SharedGenericCachedHTMLCollection<traversal kind>`, whose `elementMatches()` looks at `type()` when it runs. The type traits of the two shared classes list their types, so a type that changes groups has to be moved there too. _Why:_ Ten of 14 instantiations become two (about 32 KB). A shared collection that walks descendants is 20 to 45% slower per walk, so a type that turns out to be hot should get its own instantiation back.
- `HTMLAnchorElement.cpp`: `handleClick()` (also for `<area>`) marks the event handled and calls `window->location().navigate(href(), HistoryHandling::Push)`. It does not navigate when `target`, or else `<base target>`, is anything but `""`, `_self`, `_parent` or `_top`. It does not look at `download`. _Why:_ Only this window can be navigated, and `Location::navigate()` only follows fragment changes.
- `HTMLAnchorElement.{h,cpp}`, `HTMLFormControlElement.cpp`: `HTMLAnchorElement::isMouseFocusable()` is upstream's branch for ports other than GTK and WPE, and its `isKeyboardFocusable()` override is gone. `HTMLFormControlElement::isMouseFocusable()` is the GTK and WPE branch, and its `isKeyboardFocusable()` without `tabindex` is `isFocusable()`. _Why:_ For form controls, upstream's `#if` would pick the macOS rule. The "tab to links" and "tab to all controls" preferences live in `EventHandler`.
- `HTMLBodyElement.cpp`, `HTMLElement.cpp`: The tables of event handler attribute names are `domClientData().windowEventHandlerNames()` and `htmlEventHandlerNames()`, filled on first use, instead of `static NeverDestroyed` maps. Both lookups first return for a name that does not start with `on`. _Why:_ The tables hold atoms, so each VM needs its own. An ordinary attribute change does not pay for `domClientData()`.
- `HTMLCanvasElement.{h,cpp}`, `HTMLEmbedElement.{h,cpp}`, `HTMLObjectElement.{h,cpp}`, `HTMLFrameSetElement.{h,cpp}`, `HTMLMediaElement.{h,cpp}`, `HTMLAudioElement.{h,cpp}`, `HTMLVideoElement.{h,cpp}`, `HTMLTrackElement.{h,cpp}`, `TimeRanges.{h,cpp}`: Written by hand under upstream's file names: do not copy upstream's text over them. None derives from `ActiveDOMObject`, `CanvasBase` or `HTMLPlugInElement`, so `<object>` and `<embed>` never have a frame. `HTMLObjectElement` keeps `FormListedElement` with upstream's text for it, and `HTMLFrameSetElement` keeps upstream's `attributeChanged()` for window event handlers. `TimeRanges` is always empty and is a `ScriptWrappable`, and `is<HTMLMediaElement>()` tests the two tag names. _Why:_ Upstream's classes need graphics, plug-ins, nested browsing contexts and the media engine. The media behavior is modeled on jsdom.
- `HTMLCollection.cpp`: `invalidateNamedElementCache()` and `memoryCost()` are `NEVER_INLINE`. _Why:_ They were inlined, with their locks, into 25 instantiations each.
- `HTMLCollection.h`: `WTF_DECLARE_OWNER_THREAD_ASSERTIONS(m_namedElementCacheAssignmentLock, anyThreadLike)`, instead of `mainThreadLike`. _Why:_ The DOM works on every thread.
- `HTMLCollection.{h,cpp}`, `CachedHTMLCollectionInlines.h`: The body of `CachedHTMLCollection<>::namedItem()` is `HTMLCollection::namedItemMatching()`, which takes the kind of traversal and a function that says whether an element matches. _Why:_ One copy instead of 25 (36 KB).
- `HTMLDetailsElement.{h,cpp}`, `HTMLSummaryElement.cpp`: There is no user-agent shadow tree. `isActiveSummary()` tests for the first `<summary>` child, and `detailsElement()` is the parent element. An SVG `<a>` counts as interactive content through `elementName() == ElementNames::SVG::a`. _Why:_ Script cannot see that tree, and a `<details>` is one allocation instead of six nodes and a slot assignment. `SVGAElement` is not in Bun.
- `HTMLDocument.{h,cpp}`: `isCaseSensitiveAttribute()` and its `static NeverDestroyed` set of names are gone. `namedItem()` has no `Ref<WindowProxy>` member and no `<iframe>` branch. A document without a window has no named properties. _Why:_ Bun's CSS parser decides the case rule of each attribute selector, with `HTML_CASE_INSENSITIVE_ATTRIBUTES` in `src/css/selectors/parser.rs`. There is no frame behind an `<iframe>`. In Chrome 143 and jsdom, `<img name=body>` does not shadow `body` on what `DOMParser` or `createHTMLDocument()` made, and tests define such properties themselves to stand for it.
- `HTMLElement.h`: `hasTagName(const HTMLQualifiedName&)` is `elementName() == name.nodeName()`, instead of `hasLocalName(name.localName())`. _Why:_ A static name holds a `NodeName` and no strings. Its strings are a per-VM lookup.
- `HTMLFormElement.cpp`: `submit()` makes no `FormSubmission`. It reads the method from the form or from the submitter's `formmethod`, then calls `submitDialog()`, or `constructEntryList()` on a new `DOMFormData`. `submitIfPossible()`, `submit()` and `reset()` have no "has a frame" test: `if (!document().hasBrowsingContext()) return;` at the top of the three would restore it. _Why:_ Nothing navigates, and there is no frame.
- `HTMLFormElement.cpp`: `submit()` always resets `m_shouldSubmit` and `m_isSubmittingOrPreparingForSubmission` at its end. _Why:_ Upstream returns early and leaves the second flag set when a `formdata` listener disconnects the form.
- `HTMLFormElement.cpp`: `submitIfPossible()` always validates unless `novalidate` or `formnovalidate` is set. `validateInteractively()` only focuses the first focusable invalid control. _Why:_ `interactiveFormValidationEnabled` is taken as true. Upstream's `WebCore` default is false, but every shipping port turns it on.
- `HTMLFrameElementBase.{h,cpp}`: Derives from `HTMLElement` and has what is left of `HTMLFrameOwnerElement`: `contentWindow()`, `contentDocument()` and `disconnectContentFrame()`, on a `RefPtr<Window>` in place of the weak pointer to a `Frame`. `attributeChanged()`, `insertionSteps()`, `postConnectionSteps()` and `setLocation()` are upstream's text less the loader. `openURL()` is new: it closes the old window, makes a new one and fills its document from `srcdoc` or with an empty page. `removingSteps()` is new too and disconnects the window. _Why:_ Only `<iframe>` and `<frame>` own a frame. Upstream disconnects the frames of a subtree in `ContainerNode`, before it removes the subtree, so that `unload` listeners can run, and keeps a count of frames in every ancestor for that. Nothing fires `unload` here.
- `HTMLIFrameElement.{h,cpp}`, `HTMLFrameElement.{h,cpp}`: Upstream's text less rendering, lazy loading, sandbox flags and fullscreen. `srcdoc` is a reflected attribute.
- `HTMLIFrameElement.cpp`, `HTMLLinkElement.cpp`: Two tables are copied from files that are not in Bun: the twelve sandbox tokens from `SecurityContext::isSupportedSandboxPolicy()`, and `supportedLinkTypes` from `linkTypes` in `LinkRelAttribute.cpp`. The second has no `compression-dictionary`, `manifest`, `preconnect` and `prefetch`, and `as()` does not accept `video` and `audio`. _Why:_ Keep both in sync with upstream. What is left out is off in upstream's defaults.
- `HTMLInputElement.{h,cpp}`: New override `supportsFocus()`: false for `type=hidden`. _Why:_ Upstream needs no such rule: a hidden input has no renderer, and `isFocusable()` asks for one.
- `HTMLScriptElement.{h,cpp}`: `setText(Variant)`, `setTextContent(std::optional<Variant>)`, `setTextContent(ExceptionOr<String>)` and `setInnerText(Variant)` are gone. The bindings call `setText(String&&)`, `Node::setTextContent()` and `HTMLElement::setInnerText()`. `setSrc()` is `void setSrc(String&&)`. _Why:_ No trusted types.
- `HTMLSelectElement.cpp`, `HTMLOptionElement.cpp`, `HTMLOptGroupElement.cpp`, `HTMLHRElement.cpp`, `HTMLSelectedContentElement.cpp`, `HTMLButtonElement.cpp`: `htmlEnhancedSelectParsingEnabled` and `htmlEnhancedSelectEnabled` are taken as true. `htmlEnhancedSelectMultipleAndListBoxEnabled`, `htmlEnhancedSelectMultipleSelectedContentEnabled` and `selectShowPickerEnabled` are taken as false. _Why:_ Upstream's defaults. `parser/HTMLParserOptions.h` has to use the same values.
- `HTMLTextFormControlElement.{h,cpp}`, `HTMLInputElement.cpp`, `HTMLTextAreaElement.{h,cpp}`: A text control has no inner editor: the value is `m_valueIfDirty` or `m_value`, and the selection is only the three `m_cachedSelection*` members. `setSelectionRange()` clamps to `value()->length()` and calls `cacheSelection()`, and `setRangeText()` reads `value()`, instead of `innerTextValue()`. `normalizeSelectionDirection()` is gone: its callers pass `SelectionHasNoDirection`, which is also the initial direction. _Why:_ There is no shadow tree and no `FrameSelection`. `normalizeSelectionDirection()` asked the frame's editing behavior, which differs by platform.
- `InputType.cpp`: The factory table is a `static constexpr SortedArrayMap` keyed by `ComparableCaseFoldingASCIILiteral`, instead of a `NeverDestroyed` hash map keyed by `AtomString`. Its value is `{ InputType::Type, factory }`, and `createIfDifferent()` compares `Type`s, not names. _Why:_ A process-wide map of atoms fails on a second thread. Do not use `ComparableLettersLiteral`: it folds by setting bit 0x20, so it takes `"datetime\rlocal"` for `datetime-local`.
- `InputType.cpp`: The factory table has no settings column. `color`, `date`, `datetime-local`, `month`, `time` and `week` always exist. _Why:_ Upstream's `WebCore` default for these six settings is false, but shipping ports turn them on (`week` only on iOS and GTK).
- `TextFieldInputType.cpp`: `setValue()` puts the caret at `input->value()->length()`, instead of `visibleValue().length()`. The Up and Down keys call `stepUpOrDown()`, instead of `spinButtonStepUp()` and `spinButtonStepDown()`. _Why:_ There is no visible value and no spin button. On `form.reset()` the sanitized value is null, so its length cannot be used.
- `TextFieldInputType.cpp`, `RangeInputType.cpp`: `shouldRespectListAttribute()` returns true. _Why:_ `dataListElementEnabled` is taken as true. Upstream's default is false outside Cocoa, GTK and WPE, but `<datalist>` exists in every browser.
- `ValidityState.h`, `FormListedElement.{h,cpp}`: `ValidityState` is a real class: a `ScriptWrappable` with a reference to its element, to which `ref()` and `deref()` forward. `FormListedElement` owns it lazily in `m_validity`. Upstream casts the `FormListedElement` itself. _Why:_ Wrapper identity comes from `ScriptWrappable`. Making `FormListedElement` one would give every control two such bases.

### html/parser/

Preloading, byte decoding, script execution, text documents, `srcset` parsing, srcdoc documents and telephone number detection are cut, with the files, base classes and members that served them. The input is always a complete string, so the parser never yields: there is no scheduler, `SynchronousMode` or `PumpSession`, and each entry point returns when the input is used up.

- `HTMLConstructionSite.cpp`: `findBreakIndexSlow()` opens ICU's character break iterator itself with `ubrk_open()`, instead of `NonSharedCharacterBreakIterator`, and declares the four `ubrk_` functions where `<unicode/ubrk.h>` is missing. _Why:_ The macOS SDK has no `ubrk.h`, and `<wtf/text/TextBreakIterator.h>` includes it.
- `HTMLDocumentParser.cpp`: `runScriptsForPausedTreeBuilder()` calls `scriptElement->prepareScript(position)` itself, instead of `HTMLScriptRunner::execute()`. `prepareToStopParsing()` calls `end()`, instead of `attemptToRunDeferredScriptsAndEnd()`. _Why:_ No script runs. The call only makes the element "already started".
- `HTMLDocumentParser.cpp`: `runScriptsForPausedTreeBuilder()` has no `performMicrotaskCheckpoint()` call. It calls `constructElementWithFallback()` without `ParserConstructElementWithEmptyStack::Yes`. _Why:_ The standard runs the checkpoint only if the JavaScript execution context stack is empty. In Bun script always calls the parser, so the stack is never empty.
- `HTMLDocumentParserFastPath.{h,cpp}`: `NewlineThenWhitespaceStringsTable` is an ordinary class in the header, instead of a class of statics in the `.cpp` file, and each VM has one. The parser reads it from `domClientData(vm)` once per parse and passes it to `ScanTextResult::tryUseWhitespaceCache()`. _Why:_ Nothing process-wide may hold a `String`. All threads would also update the reference counts of the same 33 strings.
- `HTMLNameCache.{h,cpp}`, `AtomHTMLToken.h`, `HTMLDocumentParser.{h,cpp}`, `HTMLDocumentParserFastPath.cpp`: `HTMLNameCache` is an ordinary class with two member arrays, instead of static functions over two `static MainThreadNeverDestroyed` arrays, and each VM has one. Both parsers read `domClientData(vm).htmlNameCache()` once per parse into `m_nameCache`, and the constructor of `AtomHTMLToken` takes it. _Why:_ The arrays hold `AtomString`s and `QualifiedNameImpl`s, which belong to one thread. One lookup per parse is cheaper than one per attribute.
- `HTMLParserOptions.h`: The struct that each parser fills from `Settings` becomes five `static constexpr` members: `scriptingFlag = false`, `usePreHTML5ParserQuirks = false`, `enhancedSelect = true`, `enhancedSelectQuirk = false`, `maximumDOMTreeDepth = 512`. `HTMLElementStack.cpp` and the fast path read them too. _Why:_ The tests of `m_options` keep upstream's text and fold away at compile time, so the "in select" insertion modes are dead code. Change `scriptingFlag` together with `entityMaskForText()` in `editing/MarkupAccumulator.cpp`.
- `HTMLTokenizer.{h,cpp}`: `updateStateFor(const AtomString& tagName)` becomes `updateStateFor(ElementName)`: a `switch` over the same ten names with the same states. `HTMLDocumentParser` passes `contextElement.elementName()`. _Why:_ A static name such as `textareaTag` is a per-VM lookup in Bun. The ten `hasLocalName()` tests ran for each fragment.
- `HTMLTreeBuilder.cpp`: A `<script>` that is still open at the end of the file gets `markAlreadyStarted()`, where upstream has `notImplemented()`. The other `notImplemented()` calls are gone, and the end tag of an SVG `<script>` does not set `m_scriptToProcess`. _Why:_ The standard says so. `platform/NotImplemented.h` needs WebCore's log channels, and there is no `SVGScriptElement`.
- `HTMLTreeBuilder.{h,cpp}`: The three function-local `static NeverDestroyed` maps that adjust SVG, MathML and foreign attributes become `struct HTMLTreeBuilderAttributeMaps`, read from `domClientData().treeBuilderAttributeMaps()`. `ASSERT(isMainThread())` in the fragment constructor is gone. _Why:_ The maps hold `AtomString`s and `QualifiedName`s, so each VM needs its own. The parser runs on every thread.
- `InputStreamPreprocessor.h`: `kEndOfFileMarker` is defined here. Upstream defines it in `css/parser/CSSTokenizerInputStream.h`, which is not in Bun. _Why:_ The constant is all the HTML parser used of that header. If the header is imported later, delete one of the two definitions.

### xml/

`DOMParser`, `XMLSerializer`, `XMLErrors` and `XMLHttpRequest` are in Bun, and `parser/` has a parser of Bun's own. There is no libxml2, XPath or XSLT. Of `XMLHttpRequest`, what is cut is the console messages, the content security policy, the inspector, user gestures (with them the `dispatchEvent()` override), suspension, and the synchronous half of `createRequest()`.

- `parser/XMLDocumentParser.{h,cpp}`: Written by hand under upstream's name, with upstream's `create()` (less `IsInFrameView`), `parseDocumentFragment()` and `wellFormed()`. `XMLDocumentParserLibxml2.cpp` and `XMLDocumentParserScope.{h,cpp}` are not imported. `append()` only collects the text. `finish()` gives all of it to Bun's XML parser (`src/parsers/xml.rs`), which answers with one flat list of events (`src/parsers/xml_dom.rs`, mirrored by `parser/BunXMLParser.h`). `XMLTreeBuilder` makes the nodes from the list, as upstream's SAX callbacks do. _Why:_ Bun has an XML parser and does not link libxml2. `Document::createParser()`, `DocumentFragment::parseXML()` and `createFragmentForMarkup()` keep upstream's text.
- `parser/XMLDocumentParser.cpp`: `XMLTreeBuilder` does what Namespaces in XML adds to XML: it binds prefixes, checks qualified names and the reserved prefixes, and refuses two attributes with the same expanded name. _Why:_ libxml2 does that for upstream. Bun's parser knows XML 1.0 only.
- `parser/XMLDocumentParser.cpp`: `parseDocumentFragment()` parses `<root>`, the markup and `</root>` as a document and leaves out the events of the root. A prefix that the markup does not declare is looked up with `lookupNamespaceURI()` on the context element. _Why:_ That is the algorithm of the HTML standard. Upstream calls `xmlParseContent()` with the `xmlns:` attributes of the ancestors.
- `parser/XMLDocumentParser.cpp`: After an error the open elements get `finishParsingChildren()`, and open scripts are marked as already started. _Why:_ Upstream leaves them unfinished for good, so `:last-child` never matches in them.
- `XMLErrors.{h,cpp}`: `handleError()` takes the message as a `StringView`, and the overload with a line and a column is gone. _Why:_ The messages are not C strings.
- `DOMParser.{h,cpp}`: `parseFromString()` takes `String&&`. _Why:_ No trusted types.
- `DOMParser.{h,cpp}`: New `create(ScriptExecutionContext&)` next to `create(Document&)`, and `m_scriptExecutionContext` in place of `m_settings`. The generated constructor calls `create(Document&)` only when the constructor belongs to a window. _Why:_ A `DOMParser` can exist with no window: `import { DOMParser } from "bun:dom"`. The one of a window gives its documents that window's URL, so relative URLs resolve.
- `DOMParser.{h,cpp}`, `XMLSerializer.{h,cpp}`: Both classes derive from `ScriptWrappable` and have the `TZone` allocation macros. _Why:_ Bun's wrapper cache is only the inline one (see `JSDOMWrapperCache.h`).
- `XMLHttpRequest.{h,cpp}`: The loader is `XMLHttpRequestLoader` in place of `ThreadableLoader`, and the class does not derive from `ThreadableLoaderClient`. `didSendData()`, `didReceiveResponse()`, `didReceiveData()`, `didFinishLoading()` and `didFail()` keep their names and lose the identifiers, the metrics and the `ResourceError`. `m_response` is an `XMLHttpRequestLoader::Response`, `m_requestEntityBody` a `BlobRefPtr`, `m_binaryResponseBuilder` a `Vector<uint8_t>` and `m_url` a `URL`. `handleCancellation()`, `abortError()`, `notifyIsDone()` and `m_wasDidSendDataCalledForTotalBytes` are gone. _Why:_ `loader/` and `platform/network/` are not in Bun. The request goes out through Bun's `fetch()`.
- `XMLHttpRequest.{h,cpp}`: New `create(Document&)` next to `create(ScriptExecutionContext&)`, `m_document`, and `encodingParseURL()`, whose base is `about:blank` without a document. The generated constructor calls `create(Document&)` only when the constructor belongs to a window. Every `context->isDocument()` is taken as true. `open()` also throws when the window is closed. `visitAdditionalChildrenInGCThread()` adds the document as an opaque root. _Why:_ Bun's context is not a document, and the class can exist with no window. In a browser the window outlives the request.
- `XMLHttpRequest.cpp`: `prepareToSend()` returns `NotSupportedError` for a synchronous request. _Why:_ Bun never blocks on a promise from a host function.
- `XMLHttpRequest.{h,cpp}`: `m_timeoutTimer` is a `RunLoop::Timer`. `timeoutTimerFired()` posts a task with `postTaskConcurrently()`, and the task calls `didReachTimeout()` if the same loader is still at work. `setTimeout()` starts the timer with at least 1 ms. _Why:_ `WebCore::Timer` has no implementation in Bun, and this timer is on the real clock under fake timers. Bun's loop fires it where script cannot run, sometimes right before it sleeps, and only a task posted that way wakes it. The loop has one slot for timers that are due at once.
- `XMLHttpRequest.cpp`: `stop()` also clears the send flag and sets the state to `UNSENT`. _Why:_ `Window::close()` stops a window's requests while the context lives on, and `virtualHasPendingActivity()` would keep the wrapper forever.
- `XMLHttpRequest.cpp`: `createDecoder()` makes an `XMLHttpRequestTextDecoder` from the final charset, one that also reads the XML declaration where upstream's decoder is for `application/xml`, and one that is always UTF-8 for `json`. `finalResponseCharset()` returns the label. _Why:_ There is no `TextResourceDecoder` and no `PAL::TextEncoding` registry. Upstream lets the charset decide for `json` too, which the standard does not.
- `XMLHttpRequest.cpp`: `responseXML()` asks for an XML or HTML type whatever the scheme of the URL, and `send(Blob)` has no branch for URLs that are not HTTP. `responseMIMEType()` always reads the `Content-Type` header. `getAllResponseHeaders()` copies the headers in a loop. _Why:_ Bun's `fetch()` gives `data:`, `blob:` and `file:` responses that header. The iterator of Bun's `HTTPHeaderMap` does not work with `WTF::map()`.
- `XMLHttpRequestLoader.{h,cpp}`: New. It calls the host function behind `fetch` (`Bun__fetch`) with an options object that has no prototype, reads the `Response` through the functions behind its getters (`ResponsePrototype__getStatus` and so on) and the body through the C++ stream operations, and waits with `DOMPromise::whenPromiseIsSettled()`. Each step then queues a task (`Document::queueTask()` or `postTask()`) that calls the request. `cancel()` aborts an `AbortSignal` of its own and cancels the reader. While it loads it holds a reference on the event loop and a `Window::PendingTask`, and is in `Window::loadingRequests()`. `Response` has the members of `ResourceResponse` that the request reads, under the same names. _Why:_ A script that replaces `fetch`, `Response.prototype` or `Headers.prototype` must change nothing.
- `XMLHttpRequestLoader.cpp`: It calls `didSendData(length, length)` once, right before `didReceiveResponse()`, and `didReceiveData()` with no bytes right after. _Why:_ `fetch()` does not report what it has sent. The empty call moves the state to `HEADERS_RECEIVED` when the headers are there, as the standard says. Upstream waits for the first bytes of the body.
- `XMLHttpRequestTextDecoder.{h,cpp}`: New, in place of `TextResourceDecoder`. It looks for a byte order mark, then takes the label, then UTF-8, and decodes piece by piece with `streamingUTF8Decode()` or `TextDecoder__decodeForStream()`. One made with `createForXML()` then looks for an XML declaration, with upstream's `findXMLEncoding()` and the XML half of `checkForHeadCharset()`, in the first 1,024 bytes. None looks for a `<meta charset>`.
- `XMLHttpRequestProgressEventThrottle.{h,cpp}`: Nothing is throttled or deferred: `updateProgress()` dispatches at once. The timer, `flushProgressEvent()`, `dispatchThrottledProgressEventIfNeeded()`, `suspend()`, `resume()` and `ProgressEventAction` are gone. The class stays for the numbers that `load` and `loadend` report. _Why:_ There is no `EventLoop` with repeating tasks. A test sees one `progress` for each chunk.
- `XMLHttpRequestProgressEventThrottle.cpp`, `XMLHttpRequestUpload.cpp`: The events are `ProgressEvent`s. `XMLHttpRequestProgressEvent` is not imported. _Why:_ Only WebKit has that class.
- `XMLHttpRequestUpload.h`: New `request()`. _Why:_ `Window::forEventTarget()` needs the window of an upload.

### editing/

Only `markup.{h,cpp}` and `MarkupAccumulator.{h,cpp}` are in Bun, cut to `serializeFragment()`, `createFragmentForInnerOuterHTML()`, `createContextualFragment()` and `replaceChildrenWithFragment()`. The pasteboard, sanitizing, `StyledMarkupAccumulator`, URL replacement, exclusion rules and XSLT parts are gone.

- `MarkupAccumulator.cpp`: In XML, `appendStartTag()` records the namespace declarations of the element before it writes the first attribute. _Why:_ Upstream writes `xmlns:p` twice for `<a p:x="" xmlns:p="urn:p"/>`. libxml2 hides that by handing over the declarations first. Bun's parser keeps the order of the source.
- `MarkupAccumulator.cpp`: `entityMaskForText()` has no `noscript` case, and `isScriptEnabled()` is gone. _Why:_ Scripting counts as disabled, as in the parser. Change it together with `HTMLParserOptions::scriptingFlag`.

### loader/

Only `FormSubmission.{h,cpp}` is in Bun. Nothing is loaded or navigated.

- `FormSubmission.{h,cpp}`: `FormSubmission` is a plain holder of `enum class Method` and `class Attributes` (method and encoding type only), instead of a ref-counted request. `enum FormSubmissionTrigger` is defined here, because `FormState.h` is not in Bun. _Why:_ The class is kept so that `FormSubmission::Attributes::...` in `HTMLFormElement` and `HTMLFormControlElement` stays upstream's text.

### fileapi/

Only `FileList`, `FileReader` and its loader are in Bun, and `Blob` is Bun's own class. `FileReader.{h,cpp}` and `FileReaderLoaderClient.h` are upstream's text, less logging and what Bun's `Blob` and `DOMException` do not have.

- `FileList.{h,cpp}`: `Ref<File>`, `File*` and `const File&` become `Ref<Blob>`, `Blob*` and `Blob&`. _Why:_ Bun's C++ has no `File`: a file is a `Blob` with a name.
- `FileReader.{h,cpp}`: The counter behind the task identifiers is a member, `m_taskIdentifierSeed`, instead of a `static` in `enqueueTask()`. _Why:_ All threads incremented the static without synchronization, and a lost update could give one reader the same identifier twice.
- `FileReaderLoader.cpp`: Text is decoded by Bun's `TextDecoder` through `TextDecoder__createForStream()` and its two companions. The order is upstream's: byte order mark, the label given, the `charset` of the blob's type, UTF-8. A rejected read is `NotFoundError` when the error's `code` is `"ENOENT"`, else `NotReadableError`. _Why:_ There is no `TextResourceDecoder`. The error comes from Bun's file system code, not from a network response.
- `FileReaderLoader.{h,cpp}`: Written anew with upstream's public names. It calls the native function behind `Blob.prototype.arrayBuffer` (`BlobPrototype__getArrayBuffer`), waits with `DOMPromise::whenPromiseIsSettled()`, then posts one task that stores the bytes and calls the client. It reads the blob's type itself, so `FileReader.cpp` does not call `setDataType()`. _Why:_ Upstream loads the blob's URL through the network stack. This way every kind of Bun blob works, and a script that replaces `Blob.prototype.arrayBuffer` changes nothing. Without the task, `loadstart` would already report all bytes as loaded.

### storage/

Only `Storage` and `StorageEvent` are in Bun. Nothing fires a `storage` event, so `StorageEvent` has no native `create()`.

- `Storage.{h,cpp}`: New text under upstream's name: a `HashMap` of items, a `Vector` of keys in insertion order and a size count for the quota. There is one object per window and area, where upstream wraps a `StorageArea`. _Why:_ Storage is in memory and nothing shares it.

### animation/

Only `CSSAnimationEvent`, `CSSTransitionEvent` and their base class are in Bun. There is no `WebAnimation`, so every member that takes or returns one is gone.

- `StyleOriginatedAnimationEvent.{h,cpp}`: The class derives from `Event`, instead of `AnimationEventBase`. `pseudoElement()` returns the string that the init dictionary gave. _Why:_ The rest of `animation/` is cut, and so is style resolution.

### svg/

Bun has the classes that jsdom has: `SVGElement`, `SVGGraphicsElement`, the elements `svg`, `g`, `defs`, `desc`, `metadata`, `switch`, `symbol` and `title`, and seven kinds of values. Nothing is drawn or animated, so renderers, `SVGPropertyRegistry`, the animators and all of `properties/` but three headers are gone. Each element class is upstream's text cut down to `create()`, the constructor and `supportsFocus()`.

- `SVGElement.{h,cpp}`: New text under upstream's name. It is the base class, and with `create()` the concrete class of every tag that has none of its own. It derives from `StyledElement` only, and keeps `ownerSVGElement()`, `viewportElement()`, `tabindex` and the event handler attributes. Elements in the MathML namespace are plain `Element`s. _Why:_ Scripts expect `style`, `dataset`, `focus()` and `on*` of any SVG element.
- `properties/SVGAnimatedString.{h,cpp}`, `properties/SVGAnimatedPropertyImpl.h`, `properties/SVGProperty.h`, `SVGRect.{h,cpp}`, `SVGPreserveAspectRatio.{h,cpp}`, `SVGStringList.{h,cpp}`, `SVGNumber.h`, `SVGFitToViewBox.h`: New text under upstream's names: do not copy upstream's text over them. A value that belongs to an element holds a `Ref` to it and no state: it parses the content attribute at each read and writes the attribute at each change. `animVal` is a read-only view of the same attribute. The element holds nothing: `classNameAnimated()`, `viewBoxAnimated()`, `requiredExtensions()` and the like make a new object, and `[CachedAttribute]` in `idl/` keeps it in the element's wrapper. All derive from `ScriptWrappable`. `SVGRect::Value` stands in for `FloatRect`, and `SVGFitToViewBox` is a template without members. _Why:_ Upstream allocates an `SVGAnimatedString` with every SVG element and five more objects with every `<svg>`, keeps a second copy of each value for animation, and writes attributes back lazily through a process-wide registry keyed by `QualifiedName`. Here an element that script never asks costs nothing.
- `SVGSVGElement.cpp`: `getElementById()` walks the descendants, and `suspendRedraw()` returns 1. `SVGTitleElement` does not tell the document about itself. _Why:_ The tree scope's map has connected elements only, and jsdom finds the others too. 1 is what SVG 2 and jsdom say. `document.title` knows the HTML `<title>` only.
- `SVGGraphicsElement.{h,cpp}`: `SVGTests` is not a base class: its two lists are members here. _Why:_ Nothing evaluates conditional processing.
- `SVGParserUtilities.{h,cpp}`, `SVGPreserveAspectRatioValue.{h,cpp}`: Upstream's text, cut to `parseNumber()` on a buffer with its helpers, and to parsing and serializing. `parseViewBox()` in `SVGRect.cpp` is `SVGFitToViewBox::parseViewBoxGeneric()`.

### css/

C++ keeps a CSS value as text and never looks inside it, so there are no `CSSValue` classes, typed values, `calc()` trees, Typed OM, or font, keyframe and counter-style code, and nothing takes a `CSSParserContext`. Nothing is loaded, so a sheet has no origin check, `replace()`, adopting tree scopes or copy on write. The selector files (`CSSSelector.*`, `CSSSelectorList.*`, `SelectorChecker*`, `SelectorFilter.*`) are upstream's text cut to what a query needs, and selector text comes from the printer in `src/css/`.

- `CSSRule.*`, `CSSRuleList.*`, `CSSConditionRule.h`, `CSSGroupingRule.*`, `CSSLayerBlockRule.h`, `CSSLayerStatementRule.h`, `CSSMediaRule.*`, `CSSStyleRule.*`, `CSSSupportsRule.h`, `CSSStyleSheet.*`, `StyleSheet.*`, `StyleSheetContents.*`, `StyleSheetList.*`, `StyleRule.*`, `CSSProperty.h`, `StyleProperties.*`, `ImmutableStyleProperties.h`, `MutableStyleProperties.*`, `MediaList.*`: New text under upstream's names, without upstream's license comment. Do not copy upstream's text over them. `StyleSheet`, `CSSRule`, `CSSRuleList`, `MediaList` and `StyleSheetList` also derive from `ScriptWrappable`. _Why:_ Values, selectors, preludes and media queries are text from the Rust parser. Bun's wrapper cache has no per-world map: only a `ScriptWrappable` keeps its wrapper.
- `CSSProperty.h`, `StyleProperties.cpp`: A declaration is an id, a `String` value, a custom property name, an important bit and a `RefPtr<CSSShorthandValue>`. The longhands of one shorthand declaration share that new object, which keeps the shorthand's text and, with `var()` in it, plays upstream's pending-substitution value. Otherwise a shorthand is put together from its longhands by its `ShorthandPattern`, in place of upstream's `ShorthandSerializer`. _Why:_ `style.margin` answers with the declared text while all its longhands still come from that one declaration.
- `CSSPropertyNames.{h,cpp}`: Both are checked in. `src/codegen/webcore/css-properties.ts` writes them and `src/css/dom/properties.rs` from upstream's `CSSProperties.json` and `UnifiedWebPreferences.yaml`. Upstream makes them at build time with `process-css-properties.py` and gperf. _Why:_ The property ids in C++ and in Rust have to agree.
- `CSSPropertyNames.{h,cpp}`: The script decides which properties exist. A setting counts as on if the YAML says `true` by default or for Cocoa, and so do six more: `cssUnprefixedBackdropFilterEnabled`, `cssScrollbarColorEnabled`, `cssOverflowClipMarginEnabled`, `cssTextJustifyEnabled`, `cssFontVariantEmojiEnabled`, `cssDPropertyEnabled`. Of the build defines, `ENABLE_VARIATION_FONTS`, `ENABLE_DARK_MODE_CSS` and `ENABLE_CSS_TAP_HIGHLIGHT_COLOR` count as on. `ENABLE_APPLE_PAY`, `ENABLE_CURSOR_VISIBILITY`, `ENABLE_SPATIAL_PORTAL`, `ENABLE_WEBKIT_OVERFLOW_SCROLLING_CSS_PROPERTY`, `ENABLE_WEBKIT_TOUCH_CALLOUT_CSS_PROPERTY` and `HAVE_CORE_MATERIAL` count as off. _Why:_ There is no `Settings` class, and nothing can change a setting at run time. At least two of WebKit, Chromium and Firefox ship the six.
- `CSSPropertyNames.{h,cpp}`: A shorthand that Bun's CSS parser cannot expand counts as a longhand. Initial values are text in computed form (`rgb(0, 0, 0)`, `16px`), and the ones that depend on layout are a keyword or a percentage (`width: auto`, `transform-origin: 50% 50%`). _Why:_ There is no `RenderStyle` to ask.
- `CSSSelector.h`, `SelectorChecker.cpp`: `AttributeMatchType::Default` means "no flag, on an attribute whose value HTML compares case-insensitively". A selector with no flag on any other attribute is `CaseSensitive`, and `checkOne()` does not call `HTMLDocument::isCaseSensitiveAttribute()`. _Why:_ Bun's parser classifies each attribute selector once. That function's static set of `AtomString`s cannot exist in Bun.
- `CSSStyleProperties.cpp`, `StyleAttributeMutationScope.h`: The cache of `getCSSPropertyIDFromJavaScriptPropertyName()` is per VM, in `DOMClientData::cssPropertyIDsByJavaScriptName()`, instead of two `NeverDestroyed` maps. `StyleAttributeMutationScope` has no `s_scopeCount`, no `s_currentScope` and no `.cpp` file. _Why:_ No process-wide state: Bun has one VM per thread, and each can have its own DOM.
- `MediaList.{h,cpp}`, `MediaQueryList.{h,cpp}`: `MediaQueries { String text; bool matches; }` replaces `MQ::MediaQueryList` everywhere. `MediaList` splits and joins the serialized text. `MediaQueryList` is not an `ActiveDOMObject`, and `matches()` returns the value from the start. _Why:_ Rust parses, serializes and judges a media query list. Nothing about the medium ever changes.
- `SelectorChecker.{h,cpp}`: The checker has one mode, upstream's `QueryingRules`: `Mode`, `MatchType`, `MatchResult` and `doesNotMatchDuringParsing()` are gone, and `CheckingContext` and `LocalContext` keep only what that mode reads. `CheckingContext::mustMatchHostPseudoClass` is new: `match()` tests it where upstream tests `styleScopeOrdinal == Style::ScopeOrdinal::Shadow`. The static `computeHasTraversalType()` replaces `Style::computeHasArgumentRelation()`. _Why:_ There is no style resolution and no invalidation. The cascade in `style/StyleExtractor.cpp` uses the same mode and sets the flag for rules from the element's own shadow tree. `LocalContext` is copied at each step of a match.
- `SelectorChecker.cpp`: `tagMatches()` finds `*` by looking at the string (`isStar()`). It does not read `anyQName()` or `starAtom()`. _Why:_ It is the hottest test, and those two are per-VM lookups in Bun.
- `SelectorChecker.cpp`: `:nth-last-child(An+B of S)` always tests that the element itself matches S. Upstream tests it only if the parent is an `Element`. _Why:_ This fixes a bug of upstream. `:nth-child` has no such condition.
- `SelectorChecker.cpp`: The pseudo-classes of cut features are `case` labels that return false. `Match::PseudoElement` and the three shadow relations end in `ASSERT_NOT_REACHED()`. _Why:_ `src/css/selectors/dom.rs` never emits them. What is valid but cannot match in Bun, such as a selector with a pseudo-element, `:autofill`, `:playing` or `:dir(x)`, arrives as `:not(*)`.
- `StyleProperties.cpp`, `MutableStyleProperties.cpp`: `all` is stored as one declaration instead of being expanded. `findDeclarationForCascade()`, `serializeAll()`, `removePropertiesOverriddenByAll()` and `isAffectedByAll()` make everything else answer as if it were expanded. _Why:_ One declaration is cheaper than about 500.
