- `StyleRule.{h,cpp}`, `CSSGroupingRule.{h,cpp}`, `CSSTextRule.h`: Three classes replace upstream's about twenty: `StyleRule`, which holds its nested rules itself, `StyleRuleGroup` (`@media`, `@supports`, `@layer {}`, `@container`, `@scope`, `@starting-style`) and `StyleRuleText` (every other at-rule, kept as text). `CSSGroupingRule` is concrete and wraps the groups that have no class of their own, and `CSSTextRule` is new. `CSSLayerBlockRule.h` and `CSSLayerStatementRule.h` are new text that reads the prelude. _Why:_ A group holds its prelude as text and whether its condition is true. An at-rule that has no effect without rendering only has to show `type` and `cssText`.
- `StyleRule.h`, `CSSStyleRule.cpp`: `StyleRule::Selectors` is the `CSSSelectorList` without pseudo-elements, one `PseudoElementType` per complex selector, and the serialized text, which `selectorText()` returns. `PseudoElementType` is defined here with the numbers of `src/css/dom`: change both together. _Why:_ Rust takes the pseudo-element off each selector and serializes the list.

### css/parser/

Bun parses CSS with its own Rust code in `src/css/`: one CSS parser in the binary is enough. Upstream's tokenizer, `CSSParserImpl`, the property parsers, `CSSSelectorParser` and the generated name tables are not imported.

- `BunCSSParser.h`: New. It mirrors every type and number of `src/css/dom/mod.rs`, with `static_assert`s on sizes and offsets. _Why:_ It is the C++ side of the ABI. Change both together.
- `BunSelectorParser.{h,cpp}`: New, in place of `CSSSelectorParser.*`, `CSSSelectorParserContext.*` and, for selectors, `CSSTokenizer`. `parseCSSSelectorList(const String&, bool inQuirksMode)` gets a flat array of ops from Rust and builds a `CSSSelectorList` through `MutableCSSSelector`. The string crosses as UTF-8, so a lone surrogate becomes U+FFFD. _Why:_ Rust decides validity and shape. `SelectorChecker`, `SelectorQuery` and `SelectorFilter` work on upstream's data structure unchanged.
- `BunSelectorParser.cpp`: The enumerations of the C ABI have Bun's own explicit numbers, mirrored in `src/css/selectors/dom.rs`: a new pseudo-class needs an entry in `BunSelectorPseudoClass`, in `toPseudoClass()` and in `PseudoClassKind` on the Rust side. `BunSelectorListBuilder` checks with `RELEASE_ASSERT` each shape the checker assumes, such as a `HasScope` at the left end of each `:has()` argument. `isEquivalentToClassSelector()` is copied from upstream's `CSSSelectorParser.cpp`. _Why:_ The values of `CSSSelector::PseudoClass` depend on `ENABLE()` flags. A bad shape would be a bad read in the checker.
- `CSSParser.{h,cpp}`: New text on the C ABI of `src/css/dom`, with upstream's static entry points and some new ones. Do not copy upstream's text over it. `CSSParsedValueCache` is new and per VM, in `DOMClientData`: it maps (property, flags, text) to the parsed longhands or "invalid", holds 512 entries and skips values over 128 characters. _Why:_ Nothing in C++ tokenizes CSS. Each call into Rust makes an arena, and React sets the same few hundred pairs again and again.

### style/

Upstream's style resolution is not imported: there is no `Style::Resolver`, `TreeResolver`, `Builder`, `ElementRuleCollector`, `RenderStyle`, invalidation or cache. Only `getComputedStyle()` reads style. All files but `HasSelectorFilter.{h,cpp}` and `SelectorMatchingState.h` are new text under upstream's names, so do not copy upstream's text over them.

- `RuleSet.{h,cpp}`, `RuleSetInlines.h`, `StyleScope.{h,cpp}`: There is one `Scope` per tree scope that has a `<style>`, in the per-VM map `DOMClientData::styleScopes()`. The first `<style>` that is inserted makes it, and it is destroyed when the last one leaves. Its `RuleSet` is rebuilt lazily after any change, and has one entry per complex selector and a bit set of the properties any rule declares. _Why:_ `Document` and `ShadowRoot` need no member for it, and a tree without style sheets costs one look at an empty table. The bit set lets a read skip matching when no rule declares the property.
- `SelectorMatchingState.h`, `../css/SelectorFilter.{h,cpp}`: `selectorFilter` and `containerQueryEvaluationState` are gone, and `SelectorFilter` keeps only the static functions that collect hashes. The `:has()` match cache and the `HasSelectorFilter` map stay. _Why:_ Queries never use the 4 KB bloom filter, which was zeroed on each call. The two that stay keep `querySelectorAll(":has(...)")` from being quadratic.
- `StyleExtractor.{h,cpp}`: It runs the cascade for one property of one element at each read and keeps nothing between reads. Upstream reads a resolved `RenderStyle`. A rule is matched only if it declares the property and could beat the winner so far. _Why:_ Selector matching is the expensive part, so it runs last and rarely.
- `UserAgentStyle.{h,cpp}`: One function, `value(const Element&, PseudoElementType, CSSPropertyID)`: a `switch` on the property and then on `ElementName`. Upstream parses `html.css` and other sheets into process-wide rule sets. _Why:_ No selectors are matched for the defaults, and there is no process-wide state.

### src/css/

This is Bun's own CSS parser and printer, in Rust, which the bundler uses too. `dom/` and `selectors/dom.rs` are new and stand in for upstream's `css/parser/`, its property parsers and its serialization of values and selectors. Their C ABI takes and returns UTF-8, keeps no state between calls and calls nothing in C++, so it is safe on every thread.

- `printer.rs`, `css_parser.rs`, `values/`, `properties/background.rs`, `properties/font.rs`, `selectors/parser.rs`, `selectors/selector.rs`: Three switches are new, and only the DOM sets them: `Printer::cssom`, `ParserOpts::NO_UNITLESS_LENGTHS` and `ParserFlags::UNFORGIVING_SELECTORS`. With the first, the printer writes as the CSSOM does: `0px`, `0.5`, `rgb(255, 0, 0)` or the author's color keyword, `:nth-child(2n+1)`. `parse_named_color()` is ASCII case-insensitive now, which the bundler sees too. _Why:_ Bun's printer minimizes, which matches no engine. Apart from `color: RED`, the bundler's output does not change.
- `dom/properties.rs`, `dom/declarations.rs`: Each property has a `Syntax`: `Typed` and `TypedVerbatim` (checked by Bun's `Property::parse`), `Simple`, `Tokens`, `Verbatim`, `Expanded` (five shorthands taken apart here) and `All`. One pass over the tokens comes first: it accepts anything with `var()` or `env()`, handles the CSS-wide keywords and collects the color keywords. The script of `css/CSSPropertyNames.{h,cpp}` writes `properties.rs`. _Why:_ Bun's typed parsers do not know the CSS-wide keywords, and its printer would write `red` as a number.
- `dom/stylesheet.rs`: It drives Bun's `StyleSheetParser` with its own rule parser, not `StyleSheet::parse`. Each complex selector crosses as text plus the kind of its pseudo-element, and `x::slotted(y)` crosses as two selectors. Nesting is resolved as text: each `&` becomes `:is(<the parent's resolved list>)`, and no limit is set on how the text grows. _Why:_ `StyleSheet::parse` merges and reorders declarations for the bundler, and the CSSOM shows each one where the author put it. C++ sees ordinary selectors, and the specificity of `&` follows from `:is()`.
- `selectors/dom.rs`: `Emitter` is a whitelist: each `match` names the variants it accepts. `check_pseudo_element()` and `is_valid_after_part()` are the tables of valid pseudo-elements and of what may follow each one, and `supports_selector()` stands for `CSSSelectorParser::supportsComplexSelector()`. Upstream's settings have their default values in it. _Why:_ Bun's CSS parser lets unknown names through for the bundler, and `querySelector()` has to throw. A pseudo-class or pseudo-element that upstream adds, or a setting that it turns on, has to be added here.
- `selectors/parser.rs`: `HTML_CASE_INSENSITIVE_ATTRIBUTES` holds the same 46 names as upstream's `HTMLDocument::isCaseSensitiveAttribute()`. _Why:_ If upstream's list changes, change this one.

### page/

There are no `Frame` classes, pages, navigation, scrolling or screens, and `dom/Window.h` stands in for upstream's window classes and for what is left of a frame. `DOMSelection`, `History`, `Location`, `Navigator`, `ResizeObserver` and `Screen` are new text under upstream's names, so do not copy upstream's text over them. `Screen` answers with the window's inner size and a color depth of 24.

- `DOMSelection.{h,cpp}`: Written from the Selection API standard on top of `Range`: one `RefPtr<Range>` and a "backward" flag. `containsNode()` still uses upstream's `contains()` and `intersects()` on `SimpleRange`. _Why:_ Upstream sits on `FrameSelection` and the editing code, which is not imported.
- `History.{h,cpp}`, `Location.{h,cpp}`: `History` is also the session history: a vector of `{ URL, SerializedScriptValue }`, an index, and a generation counter that cancels queued traversals. `Location` derives from Bun's `URLDecomposition` (`src/jsc/bindings/URLDecomposition.h`), like `URL` and `<a>`: `fullURL()` is the document's URL and `setFullURL()` navigates. _Why:_ There is no `FrameLoader`, `BackForwardController` or `HistoryItem`. Only a change of the fragment goes anywhere.
- `Navigator.{h,cpp}`, `../plugins/DOMPluginArray.{h,cpp}`, `../plugins/DOMMimeTypeArray.{h,cpp}`: One class without `NavigatorBase`, with the members of jsdom's. `userAgent`, `platform`, `language`, `languages`, `hardwareConcurrency` and `onLine` answer what the runtime's `navigator` answers (`src/jsc/bindings/BunNavigator.h`), and `appVersion` is `"4.0"`. The two arrays are always empty, so they have no indexed or named getter, and `DOMPlugin` and `DOMMimeType` are not imported. Upstream's `partial interface Navigator` files are left out (`excluded` in `upstream.ts`). _Why:_ There is no page to ask. The runtime's own `Navigator` is another class, see "Window" below.
- `Performance.{h,cpp}`: Top level in Bun, Bun's own copy. `m_monotonicTimeOrigin` and `relativeTimeFromTimeOrigin(MonotonicTime)` are new, and the constructor matches `MonotonicTime`'s clock with Bun's origin timer once. _Why:_ `m_timeOrigin` is a wall clock time in Bun. An event's creation time is a `MonotonicTime`.
- `ResizeObserver.{h,cpp}`, `ResizeObserverCallback.h`: `create()` takes the callback and drops it, and `observe()`, `unobserve()` and `disconnect()` do nothing. The callback's `invoke()` takes no arguments, and there is no `ResizeObserverEntry`, `ResizeObserverSize` or `ResizeObservation`. _Why:_ An observation is reported when the size differs from the last one reported, which starts as 0 by 0, and without layout every box is 0 by 0. Libraries construct one without a guard.
- `WindowProperty.{h,cpp}`: New, in place of `LocalDOMWindowProperty`. It holds a raw `Window*` that `~Window` clears, and `document()`, which the collector calls. `Location`, `History`, `Navigator`, its two arrays, `Screen`, `Storage` and `DOMSelection` derive from it and from `ScriptWrappable`. _Why:_ Their wrappers share the document as opaque root with the window's wrapper and the nodes', so all of them live and die together.

### platform/

Only value types and small helpers are imported. There are no pickers, popups, date formats, locales or graphics (`graphics/DoublePoint.h` is the only file of `platform/graphics`). `MIMETypeRegistry.{h,cpp}` is cut to `isXMLMIMEType()`, and its table of JavaScript types is copied into `dom/ScriptElement.cpp`.

- `CommonAtomStrings.h`: The macro list stays and is where new atoms go. It also makes `enum class CommonAtomString`, and `xmlAtom()`, `starAtom()` and the others call `commonAtomString()`, which is per VM and filled on first use. `initializeCommonAtomStrings()` and `CommonAtomStrings.cpp` are gone. New atoms: `attributes`, `characterData`, `childList`, `closed`, `ltr`, `named`, `open`, `rtl`. _Why:_ Upstream has one process-wide `AtomString` for each. The new atoms replace function-local static `AtomString`s in `dom/` and `html/`.
- `LocalizedStrings.{h,cpp}`: Written by hand under upstream's names: 19 functions with upstream's signatures that return fixed English text, for two default button labels and 17 validation messages. The messages with an argument use the Cocoa and GLib text ("Value must be greater than or equal to 5"). _Why:_ Call sites stay unchanged, and nothing is localized. The fallback of other ports has no argument ("range underflow").

### platform/network/

`ParsedContentType.{h,cpp}` are upstream's text. The other files of this directory that Bun has are older copies at the top level of `webcore/`.

- `HTTPParsers.{h,cpp}`: Top level in Bun, cut to about a sixth of upstream. `extractCharsetFromMediaType()`, `isForbiddenHeaderName()`, `isForbiddenHeader()`, `isForbiddenMethod()` and `normalizeHTTPMethod()` are upstream's text. _Why:_ `FileReader.readAsText()` and `XMLHttpRequest` need them.

### bindings/

Bun has one file of this directory, and keeps it in `src/jsc/bindings/`.

- `IDLTypes.h`: `IDLStringContextTrustedScriptAdaptor` is cut, with its converters in `js/JSDOMConvertStrings.{h,cpp}`. The rest is upstream's text. _Why:_ No trusted types.

### bindings/js/

Helpers that Bun had before the DOM stayed where they were, and only what came with the DOM is in `webcore/bindings/js/`. `JSDOMExceptionHandling.*`, `JSDOMWrapper.h`, `JSDOMWrapperCache.h`, `JSDOMGlobalObject.*`, `JSDOMBinding.h`, `WebCoreOpaqueRoot*.h` and Bun's own `BunIDL*.h`, `DOMStructureSlot.h` and `DeleteCallbackDataTask.h` are in `src/jsc/bindings/`, and the other older helpers (most `JSDOMConvert*.h`, `JSDOMAttribute.h`, `JSDOMCastThisValue.h`, `JSDOMOperation*.h`, `JSDOMIterator.h`, `JSDOMConstructor*.h`, `JSDOMPromiseDeferred.h`, `JSCallbackData.*`, `JSEventListener.*`, `JSValueInWrappedObject.h`, `BufferSource.h`) are in `webcore/`. Cut as a whole: `JSExecState`, the inspector's instrumentation, every world but the normal one, frames, content security policy, cross-origin checks, trusted types, and the classes that make the window the global object (`JSDOMWindowBase`, `JSDOMWindowCustom`, `JSDOMWindowProperties`, `JSWindowProxy`, `JSLocationCustom.cpp`), which `Window`, `JSWindowCustom` and `JSWindowProperties` replace.

- `BufferSource.h`, `JSDOMConvertBufferSource.h`: Bun's copy. `VariantType` is `Variant<RefPtr<ArrayBufferView>, RefPtr<ArrayBuffer>>`, with a constructor from upstream's `Variant<Ref<...>, Ref<...>>&&`. It has a default constructor, `variant()`, `data()` and `length()`, and no `switchOn()`, `span()`, `mutableSpan()` or `byteLength()`, so `JSConverter<IDLBufferSource>` is cut. _Why:_ WebCrypto's parameter structures hold the `RefPtr` variant. Their bindings say `BufferSource(convert<IDLBufferSource>(...)).variant()`.
- `JSBlob.h`, `JSCustomElementInterface.cpp`, `JSElementInternalsCustom.cpp`: `JSBlob.h` is new, in place of the generated one. It has only the converter traits, whose `toWrapped()` returns a `RefPtr<Blob>` from `Blob::create()`. `invokeFormStateRestoreCallback()` and the union of `setFormValue()` have `Blob` where upstream has `File`. _Why:_ Bun's `Blob` is a Rust class. A `WebCore::Blob` is a handle that is made anew for each conversion. Bun's C++ cannot tell a `File` from a `Blob` (see `html/CustomElementFormValue.h`).
- `JSCallbackData.h`, `JSCallbackData.cpp`: Bun's copy. There is no `m_globalObject`: `globalObject()` is `defaultGlobalObject(callback->globalObject())`, and upstream's constructor `(callback, JSDOMGlobalObject*, owner)` ignores the global object. The static `invokeCallback()` takes a `VM&`, and returns at once when `context->isJSExecutionForbidden()`. `DeleteCallbackDataTask` is in a header of its own. _Why:_ The callback's realm may be a `node:vm` context, which has no context of its own. Bun's loop keeps draining tasks after the VM's stop is requested.
- `JSCSSStylePropertiesCustom.h`, `JSCSSStylePropertiesCustom.cpp`: New. `JSCSSStylePropertiesPrototypeBase`, the base class of the generated prototype, makes a `CustomGetterSetter` for a property name when the name is first looked up, and all of them in `getOwnPropertyNames()` and `deleteProperty()`, which then set `staticPropertiesReified`. One getter and one setter serve all names and find the property from the `PropertyName`. `JSCSSStyleProperties::put()` makes the accessor if needed and then calls `Base::put()`. _Why:_ Upstream generates an attribute for each of about 1,400 spellings and reifies them when the prototype is made. A program touches a few dozen. A store walks the structures of the prototype chain and does not ask `getOwnPropertySlot()`, and React stores before it reads.
- `JSCustomElementInterface.cpp`, `JSHTMLElementCustom.cpp`: The "active custom element constructor" map is the one of `registry.document()`, or, for a scoped registry, of the document the element is made for or lives in. The `HTMLElement` constructor reads the same map through `JSDOMConstructorBase::document()`. Upstream uses `downcast<Document>(scriptExecutionContext())` in both. _Why:_ Bun's context is not a document. Both sides have to pick the same document.
- `JSCustomElementInterface.cpp`: `upgradeElement()` declares a top exception scope, instead of a throw scope. _Why:_ It reports what the constructor throws and leaves nothing for its caller, and Bun's builds with assertions verify that every scope that can throw is checked.
- `JSCustomElementRegistryCustom.cpp`: `define()` and `whenDefined()` follow `validateCustomElementNameAndThrowIfNeeded()` with `RETURN_IF_EXCEPTION`, instead of testing what it returns. _Why:_ The same verification.
- `JSCustomElementRegistryCustom.cpp`: `define()` does not read `connectedMoveCallback`. _Why:_ `moveBeforeEnabled` is false in `bindings-rules.ts`, as upstream's default, and there is no `Settings` class. Change both together.
- `JSDOMBindingFacade.h`, `JSDOMBindingFacade.cpp`: `constructEmptyObject`, `createIteratorResultObject`, `getCallData`, `getConstructData`, `hasIteratorMethod` and `iteratorMethod` are `using JSC::...` declarations instead of wrapper functions. _Why:_ Bun's files say `using namespace JSC`, so a second function with the same signature is ambiguous.
- `JSDOMConstructor.h`, `JSDOMConstructorNotConstructable.h`, `JSDOMConstructorBase.{h,cpp}`, `JSDOMConstructorCallable.h`, `JSDOMOperation.h`: The base constructor takes a function for calls and a `Bun::ErrorCode`, and the first two templates take the code as a template parameter. A call without `new` throws "Use `new X(...)` instead of `X(...)`". `JSDOMConstructorCallable.h` is Bun's: a constructor that can also be called. `JSDOMOperation.h` defines `createNotEnoughArgumentsError` as a macro for `WebCore::createNotEnoughArgumentsErrorBun`. _Why:_ Bun's own classes need them. The errors carry Node's `code`, such as `ERR_ILLEGAL_CONSTRUCTOR` for "Illegal constructor".
- `JSDOMConstructorBase.{h,cpp}`, `JSDOMConstructorWithDocument.h`: Added: `createForWindow()`, `window()`, `document()` and `visitChildren`. `createForWindow()` copies a constructor (a new `Structure` with the same `ClassInfo` and prototype, the same native functions, name and own properties) and gives it a window. `JSWindowCustom.cpp` makes the copies on first use. `JSDOMConstructorWithDocument` is an alias of the base class, and `scriptExecutionContext()` is the global object's `currentScriptExecutionContext()`. _Why:_ The context is not a `Document`, and a realm has many windows, so a constructor that needs "the current document" has to know its window. `document()` is null for the constructor cached on the global object. What script makes in a `Bun.ModuleGraph` belongs to that graph's context.
- `JSDOMConvertBase.h`, `JSDOMConvertDictionary.h`, `JSDOMConvertEnumeration.h`, `JSDOMConvertNullable.h`, `JSDOMConvertOptional.h`, `JSDOMConvertSequences.h`, `BunIDLConvertBase.h`: The `JSDOMConvert*.h` family is upstream's text, plus Bun's context protocol as extra members: `takesContext` (false in `DefaultConverter`), `convert(globalObject, value, context)` that returns the plain value, and `tryConvert()` that returns an `optional` (`nullopt` for a dictionary when the value is not an object). Upstream's `convert()` with an exception thrower is constrained so that a context does not match it. `Nullable` and `Optional` take `conversionHasSideEffects` from the inner type. `BunIDLConvertBase.h` defines the protocol, and its `DefaultContextConverter::convert(globalObject, value)` returns a `ConversionResult<IDL>`. _Why:_ Bun's own binding generator converts through `Bun::convertIDL()` and `Bun::tryConvertIDL()`. A context gives stricter checks and "value must be ..." messages. A converter of Bun's has to fit upstream's `convert<IDL>()` too.
- `JSDOMConvertBase.h`, `JSDOMConvertStrings.{h,cpp}`: Exception checks are added: after `valueOrFunctor()` in the three `toJS()` overloads that take a functor, and between `toString()` and `toAtomString()` in the atom string converter. `valueToUSVString()` throws "Cannot convert a Symbol value to a string" for a symbol. _Why:_ An implementation function of Bun's can throw through the VM as well as through `ExceptionOr`, and exception scope verification needs the second check. The message is Node's and V8's.
- `JSDOMConvertBoolean.h`: A `convert()` that takes a context is added. It calls `toBoolean()` and declares no scope. _Why:_ `ToBoolean` never throws, so bindgen's generated code has no exception check after it. Upstream's `convert()` declares a throw scope, which the validation of exception checks then wants looked at.
- `JSDOMConvertBufferSource.cpp`: `toJS(…, ArrayBuffer&)` takes the structure from `lexicalGlobalObject`, instead of `globalObject`. _Why:_ `WebCoreTypedArrayController` passes the VM's default global as `globalObject`, so the `buffer` of a typed array made in a `node:vm` context would get the main realm's `ArrayBuffer.prototype`.
- `JSDOMConvertBufferSource.h`, `JSDOMConvertUnion.h`: `BufferSourceConverter::tryConvert()`, which only unions call, uses `toWrapped()` or `toWrappedAllowShared()` and throws nothing, so a shared buffer goes on to the next member of the union. Upstream throws "SharedArrayBuffer is not allowed" and "Resizable ArrayBuffer is not allowed" there. In the union's converter the three `toWrappedAllowSharedAndResizable()` tests for `object` are `toWrapped()`, and a resizable or growable buffer throws "ArrayBuffer cannot be resizable" or "ArrayBufferView cannot be resizable", also in a union that has `object` and no buffer type. _Why:_ Released behavior and messages of `crypto.subtle` and other Bun APIs. No union in the DOM's bindings has a buffer type, so nothing needs upstream's behavior.
- `JSDOMConvertEnumeration.h`, `JSDOMConvertSequences.h`: With a context, an enumeration refuses a value that is not a string and does not coerce it. The iterable path without a method and the array fast path of a sequence call the added `convertWithDefaultContext()`, which converts an element whose converter takes a context with `Bun::DefaultConversionContext`. `convert(object, method)`, the path of a sequence inside a union, stays without a context. `Detail::SequenceConverter` forwards a `convert()` with a context to `Bun::Detail::SequenceConverter` in `BunIDLConvertSequence.h`. _Why:_ Bun's own APIs do not coerce enumeration values: `key_ops: [["encrypt"]]` is refused in a `sequence<KeyUsage>`. `new URLSearchParams([1])` keeps its message. A nested sequence says "value must be a sequence".
- `JSDOMConvertPromise.h`: The global object is `defaultGlobalObject(&lexicalGlobalObject)` instead of a `dynamicDowncast` with a `RELEASE_ASSERT`. _Why:_ The lexical global object of a `node:vm` context is not a `JSDOMGlobalObject`. `new PromiseRejectionEvent("x", { promise })` there would crash.
- `JSDOMConvertRecord.h`: Adds a fast path for a plain object whose prototype is `Object.prototype` or null. It reads names and offsets from the structure, and goes back to `[[GetOwnProperty]]` once the structure changes. _Why:_ Speed. Bun had it before the DOM.
- `JSDOMConvertResult.h`: In `ConversionResultStorage<T&>`, the lambda of the converting constructor returns `std::expected<std::reference_wrapper<Type>, ConversionResultException>` and casts to `ReturnType`. _Why:_ Upstream's lambda returns `std::expected<Type, ...>`, which is not the type of the member it initializes.
- `JSDOMConvertResult.h`, `JSDOMConvertInterface.h`, `JSDOMConvertBufferSource.h`: `ConversionResult` gets a default constructor that means "exception", `operator ReturnType()`, and `operator*` and `operator->` for a `Ref`. A failed conversion converts to a default-constructed value. The `JSConverter`s of interfaces and typed arrays have `U*` and `const RefPtr<U>&` overloads, `toJS()` takes an `ArrayBuffer*` or an `ArrayBufferView*`, and null becomes `null`. _Why:_ The hand-kept bindings say `auto x = convert<IDL>(...); RETURN_IF_EXCEPTION(...)` and pass pointers, and older `convertDictionary()` functions say `return { };`. The members of `ConversionResult` can go when those files test `hasException()`.
- `JSDOMCSSNamespace.h`, `JSDOMCSSNamespace.cpp`: Written by hand. `CSS` is a plain object with `supports` and `escape`, one per global object. Upstream generates it from IDL. _Why:_ A namespace has no interface object and no prototype of its own.
- `JSDOMExceptionHandling.h`, `JSDOMExceptionHandling.cpp`: Bun's copy, with upstream's newer functions added as upstream's text. The functions that throw a `TypeError` for an argument, a dictionary member or `this` give it Node's `code`: `ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE`, `ERR_MISSING_OPTION`, `ERR_INVALID_THIS`, `ERR_ARG_NOT_ITERABLE`. `createDOMException()` takes an `extra` string and makes Node's errors for the codes that Bun adds to `ExceptionCode.h`, `throwSequenceTypeError()` takes a function name and an argument name, and `throwDictionaryMemberTypeError()` is Bun's. `reportException()` hands the exception to `Zig::GlobalObject::reportUncaughtExceptionAtEventLoop()`. _Why:_ Node compatibility of Bun's own classes, whose bindings call these. The DOM's bindings get the same errors. Bun has its own handling of uncaught exceptions, and `Window::reportException()` fires a window's `error` event.
- `JSDOMGlobalObject.h`, `JSDOMGlobalObject.cpp`, `JSDOMGlobalObjectInlines.h`, `JSDOMBinding.h`, `JSDOMWrapper.h`, `JSCustomElementInterface.h`: There is no `JSDOMGlobalObject` class: the name is an alias of `Zig::GlobalObject`, and the first four files are Bun's own and hold little more than `toJSDOMGlobalObject()`. A `class JSDOMGlobalObject;` in an imported header does not compile. Such a header declares `namespace Zig { class GlobalObject; }` and repeats the alias. _Why:_ Bun has one class of global object, which does that work.
- `JSDOMIterator.h`, `JSDOMPromiseDeferred.h`, `JSDOMOperationReturningPromise.h`: Bun's older copies. `iteratorCreate(wrapper, kind)` takes two arguments, the `JSDOMIteratorBase` constructor calls `createIterator()` itself, and `forEach()` with a callback that is not callable throws `ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE`. In `JSDOMPromiseDeferred.h` only `resolveWithJSValue()` comes from upstream's newer text, and `shouldIgnoreRequestToFulfill()` also asks `canInvokeCallback()`. Missing: `resolveWithNewlyCreated()`, `fulfillWithCallback()`, `whenSettledWithResult()`, `markAsHandled()`, `needsAbort()`, `callPromisePairFunction()` and with it `callReturningPromisePair()`. _Why:_ Bun's own iterables and classes depend on the older text. The DOM's bindings need nothing else.
- `JSDOMSetLike.cpp`: `forwardForEachCallToBackingSet()` iterates the backing set in C++ with `forEachInIterable()` and calls `callback(value, value, setLike)` with `this` undefined. _Why:_ Upstream calls the JS builtin `forEachWrapper` through `builtinInternalFunctions()`, which Bun's global object does not have.
- `JSDOMWrapper.h`: Bun's copy. It adds `JSAsJSONType = 0b11101100`, `JSDOMObject::globalObject()` and `protectedWrapped()`. `JSDOMErrorWrapper`, the wrapper base for `[Exception]` interfaces, and `JSDOMObject::finishCreation()` are missing. _Why:_ `JSCookie`, `JSCookieMap` and `JSURLSearchParams` use the type, and `src/jsc/JSType.rs` mirrors it. It has to stay below `JSNodeType`: DOMJIT's `branchIfNotNode()` tests `type >= JSNodeType`, and `dynamicDowncast<JSElement>` compares types.
- `JSDOMWrapperCache.h`, `DOMStructureSlot.h`, `DOMConstructors.h`, `DOMIsoSubspaces.h`, `DOMClientIsoSubspaces.h`: Bun's own design. `getDOMStructure<T>()` reads `globalObject.domStructure(DOMStructureSlotOf<T>::value)`, an array with one fixed slot for each class, where upstream looks a `ClassInfo` up in a map. The four lists, three of which upstream generates at build time, are hand-kept lists of Bun's own classes, and each includes one generated `DOMBindings*.h` list for the DOM's classes. `setSubclassStructureIfNeeded<T>()` is built on Bun's `subclassStructure()`, and Bun's own constructors call `structureForNewTarget<T>()` first and pass the structure to `createWrapper()`. _Why:_ No hash lookup for each new wrapper. Every new wrapper class needs a slot, a constructor id and subspaces, which the generator's lists provide. Reading `new.target.prototype` can throw, so Bun's own constructors do it before they make anything.
- `JSDOMWrapperCache.h`, `JSValueInWrappedObject.h`, `JSValueInWrappedObjectInlines.h`: Only the inline wrapper cache exists (`hasInlineWrapperCache`): there is no `world.wrappers()` map and no `wrapperKey()`, and a class that is not a `ScriptWrappable` or an `ArrayBuffer` gets a new wrapper each time. `JSValueInWrappedObject.h` is Bun's copy with upstream's signatures added. It has no `m_world`, `isWorldCompatible()` is true, the overloads with a `JSGlobalObject&` ignore it, and the `Inlines` header only includes the first. _Why:_ One world. An imported class whose wrapper has to keep its identity derives from `ScriptWrappable` even where upstream's does not (`DOMParser`, `XMLSerializer`).
- `JSErrorHandler.cpp`: `handleEvent()` opens a `Window::CurrentEventScope` and splits exceptions between `Window::reportException()` and `reportException()`, as `JSEventListener.cpp` does. `this` inside the handler is the window when the target has one, and the global object otherwise. _Why:_ Upstream passes the global object, which is the window there.
- `JSEvent.{h,cpp}`, `JSEventCustom.cpp`, `JSEventTarget.cpp`, `JSEventTargetCustom.h`, `JSEventInit.cpp`, `JSAddEventListenerOptions.cpp`, `JSDOMFormData.cpp`, `JSMessageEvent.cpp`, `JSWebSocket.cpp`, `JSWorker.cpp`, `JSPerformance*.cpp`, the other `JS*.cpp` in `webcore/`, `src/jsc/bindings/webcrypto/JS*.cpp`: Upstream generates all but the `Custom` files. Bun keeps older generator output and edits it by hand, and Bun's generator does not make them. They follow upstream's protocol (`ConversionResult<IDLDictionary<T>> convertDictionary<T>()`, `WTF::Variant` with `WTF::visit`, `convertEnumerationToJS(VM&, T)`, `visitJSFunctionInGCThread()`) with the help of the members added to `JSDOMConvertResult.h`. `JSAddEventListenerOptions.cpp` also reads `resistStopPropagation` from a private symbol. _Why:_ They carry Bun's own messages, coercions and error codes. A change to a helper's signature, to `Event.idl` or to `EventTarget.idl` has to be made in them by hand.
- `JSEventListener.cpp`: `handleEvent()` opens a `Window::CurrentEventScope` on the window of the event's current target (`Window::forEventTarget()`), before it looks `handleEvent` up. Upstream sets `window.event` on the `JSDOMWindow` that is the realm of the function. An exception goes to `Window::reportException()` when there is such a window, else to Bun's `reportException()`. _Why:_ The global object is not the window. The `error` event belongs at the window, not at the process.
- `JSEventListener.cpp`: After each listener, `handleEvent()` calls `vm.drainMicrotasks()` when the current target belongs to a window or is a `FileReader`, an `XMLHttpRequest` or its upload, and `!vm.isEntered()`. When a listener returns an object with a callable `then`, it calls `then` with a function that rethrows on `process.nextTick()`. _Why:_ Upstream drains in `~JSExecState`. Bun's older event targets keep their order, which is Node's. Node does the second for its `EventTarget`.
- `JSEventListener.h`, `JSEventListener.cpp`, `JSWindowEventHandlerAttribute.h`: Bun's older copy with its own changes, not upstream's current text: the world member is `m_isolatedWorld`, and a listener registers as a client of the VM only in a worker's VM. `windowEventHandlerAttribute()` and `setWindowEventHandlerAttribute()` are in the new `JSWindowEventHandlerAttribute.h` and take a `Window&`. The setter passes the window's wrapper, where upstream passes the global object. _Why:_ The file also serves `AbortSignal`, `WebSocket`, `Worker` and `ModuleGraph`, and a listener on a plain `EventTarget` must not need `HTMLElement.h`. The window's wrapper marks the function (`body.onload = f`).
- `JSHTMLElementCustom.cpp`: `constructJSHTMLElement()` takes the document from `jsConstructor->document()` instead of the context. The realm of `new.target` is found with `dynamicDowncast<JSDOMGlobalObject>` and falls back to the constructor's own realm, where upstream says `downcast`. `new.target` equal to the callee is refused, like `new.target` equal to the global object's `HTMLElement`. _Why:_ A custom element class made in a `node:vm` context aborted the process. The callee is the window's own copy of `HTMLElement` (see `JSDOMConstructorBase.h`).
- `JSLazyEventListener.cpp`: A node whose document has no window makes no listener function. Otherwise the window's wrapper is pushed on the scope chain first, with `JSWithScope`: window, document, form owner, element. The function is always compiled with `TaintedByWithScopeLexicallyScopedFeature`. _Why:_ The first stands for upstream's `if (!document->frame()) return nullptr`: scripting is disabled for a document without a browsing context, such as one from `DOMParser`. Upstream's window is the global object. Without the scope, `onclick="alert(1)"` finds nothing.
- `JSLazyEventListener.cpp`: The source position is the parser's `textPosition()`. The parameter list is always `(event)`: `(evt)` for SVG is gone. The function-local `static NeverDestroyed<const String>` values are literals. _Why:_ `ScriptController::eventHandlerPosition()` did the same. A static `String` must not be shared between threads, and the DOM works on every thread.
- `JSNodeCustom.cpp`: `JSNodeOwner::isReachableFromOpaqueRoots()` asks `GCReachableRefMap::contains(node)` and `isInCustomElementReactionQueue()` for connected nodes too. Upstream asks only `if (!node.isConnected())`. _Why:_ A task's `GCReachableRef` has to keep the wrapper and its listeners alive. A node can be connected to a document that script no longer holds, and then an event queued for it was lost.
- `JSNodeCustom.h`, `JSNodeCustom.cpp`, `JSElementCustom.cpp`, `JSHTMLElementCustom.cpp`: A new wrapper is made in the global object that the caller passes. Upstream first maps that to the global object of the node's document (`globalObjectForNode()`). Every SVG element gets `createWrapper<SVGElement>()`, and the MathML branch is gone. _Why:_ All windows of a global object share its prototypes. There is one SVG class and no MathML class.
- `JSWindowCustom.cpp`: New. `FOR_EACH_WINDOW_OPERATION` lists the operations of a window, and each window binds its own copy on first read, with the plain name. `windowOperations` in `lists.ts` is the same list: change both together. _Why:_ A function called without `this` uses its realm's global object in a browser (`const { getComputedStyle } = window`). Here a realm has many windows.
- `JSWindowCustom.h`, `JSWindowCustom.cpp`: `JSWindow::toWrapped()` is hand-written: it takes a `JSWindow`, or `globalThis` when the global object's `m_window` is set. The host function `jsFunctionSetGlobalObjectWindow(window or null)` sets that member. Every conversion of a `Window` argument goes through it: `UIEventInit.view`, `initUIEvent()`, `MessageEventInit.source`. _Why:_ Test environments have `window === globalThis`, and `new MouseEvent("click", { view: window })` has to work there.
- `JSWindowProperties.h`: `GetOwnPropertySlotIsImpure` is set next to upstream's `GetOwnPropertySlotIsImpureForPropertyAbsence`. A hit is handed out through a fresh `PropertySlot` as a plain value, so it is never cacheable. _Why:_ JSC looks at the absence flag only for the base of an access. Without the other flag a miss is cached, and hot code does not see a global appear or go away.
- `JSWindowProperties.h`, `JSWindowProperties.cpp`: New, in place of `JSDOMWindowProperties`. One object per global object sits between `Window.prototype` and `EventTarget.prototype`, and all windows of the realm share it. `getOwnPropertySlot()` order: own properties, nothing for a symbol or a VM inquiry, nothing if `EventTarget.prototype` or `Object.prototype` has the name, the global object's own property, then upstream's named items of the receiver's document. The reads of the global object under way are a linked list on the stack, with its head in `DOMClientData`. _Why:_ A window is not the global object, so this is where `window.setTimeout` and `window.Array` come from. Only own properties of the global object are read, because its prototype chain can lead back here. The list stops the recursion of a global getter that reads `window[key]`.
- `JSXMLHttpRequestCustom.cpp`: A `blob` response is wrapped with `Blob__create()`, and an `arraybuffer` response is converted as `IDLArrayBuffer`. _Why:_ Bun's `toJS()` for a `Blob` marks it as a `File`. `IDLInterface<ArrayBuffer>` finds its `toJS()` only when the headers come in one order, which a unified source does not promise.
- `src/jsc/bindings/ZigGlobalObject.h`: `WriteBarrier<JSObject> m_window` in `FOR_EACH_GLOBALOBJECT_GC_MEMBER` is the window that a global object stands for. The global object holds it strongly. _Why:_ See `JSWindowCustom.cpp`.
- `WebCoreOpaqueRoot.h`, `WebCoreOpaqueRootInlines.h`: The first adds `root(ScriptExecutionContext*)`. The second does not include `JSNodeCustomInlines.h`: a file that calls `addWebCoreOpaqueRoot(visitor, node)` includes that header itself. _Why:_ `Zig::GlobalObject` adds its context as an opaque root. `JSCustomElementRegistry` is reachable from it, so a registry's wrapper and the classes it marks live as long as the global object. Bun's own bindings include the second header and must not reach `Document.h`.

### domjit/

The text is upstream's without the tests for the normal world: `branchIfNotWorldIsNormal()` and the `worldIsNormal()` test in `toWrapper()` are gone, because Bun has one world.

- `JSDocumentDOMJIT.cpp`: `compileDocumentBodyAttribute()` and `loadLocalName()` are deleted. `Document.body` is an ordinary getter (`withoutDOMJIT` in `bindings-rules.ts`). _Why:_ The snippet compares local names with the addresses of three `AtomStringImpl`s, read on a JIT compiler thread. Names are per VM in Bun, and a compiler thread has no VM. To bring it back, compare the `NodeName` in `QualifiedNameImpl`.

## Behavior

Nothing is rendered, loaded, navigated or run. So all geometry is 0, hit tests find nothing, no resource fires `load` or `error`, no animation runs, nothing native types, clicks or edits, and there is no content security policy. The lists below have what does not plainly follow from that; the CSS parser, the CSSOM and the cascade are Bun's own code, so they differ most.

### Parsing and scripts

- **Parsing and load events.** Parsing is synchronous. `document.close()` fires `readystatechange`, `DOMContentLoaded` and `load` before it returns, the first and the last only for a document that has a window. _Elsewhere:_ WebKit can yield while it parses. With a frame it waits for subresources and fires `load` later.
- **Microtasks in the parser.** The parser performs no microtask checkpoint: not before it constructs a custom element, not at `</script>`, not before `DOMContentLoaded`. _Elsewhere:_ WebKit performs one at each of these places. The standard does so only if no script is on the stack.
- **Scripts, `<noscript>`.** No `<script>` runs, but the "already started", "parser inserted" and "force async" flags change as in WebKit, so `script.async` and clones behave the same. The scripting flag is off: the content of `<noscript>` is parsed as elements, its text is escaped when serialized, and its `display` is `inline`. _Elsewhere:_ With scripting on, the content of `<noscript>` is raw text, is serialized as written and is not displayed.
- **`DOMParser`.** The one that `bun:dom` exports needs no window, and its documents have the URL `about:blank`. For the XML types it makes an `XMLDocument`, as every browser does. _Elsewhere:_ A `DOMParser` belongs to a window. The standard and jsdom make a `Document`.
- **XML: errors.** Every error ends the parse, also one about namespaces. The `<parsererror>` has WebKit's shape and place, with one message, which is that of Bun's parser. Its line and column are where the thing in error starts, in UTF-16 code units. _Elsewhere:_ libxml2 goes on after a namespace error, so WebKit has the whole tree and may list several errors. Firefox, jsdom and the Web Platform Tests have a document with nothing but a `<parsererror>` in the namespace `http://www.mozilla.org/newlayout/xml/parsererror.xml`.
- **XML: the tree.** Attributes keep the order of the source. Comments and processing instructions in the internal subset make no nodes. _Elsewhere:_ WebKit has the namespace declarations in front of the other attributes, and nodes after the doctype for what is in the subset. Firefox and jsdom agree with Bun.
- **XML: entities.** Nothing external is read. A reference to an external entity gives nothing, and one to an entity that the internal subset does not declare is an error, whatever the doctype refers to. Expansion stops with an error at 1 MiB if that is over 100 times the size of the text. Attributes that an `ATTLIST` defaults are added. The names of HTML (`&nbsp;`) work after one of the XHTML or MathML public identifiers that WebKit knows. _Elsewhere:_ WebKit reads external entities of the same origin for a document in a frame, and its limit is a number of references, from a setting. jsdom knows only `<!ENTITY name "value">`, takes the value as text, and has neither defaults nor the names of HTML.

### Loading and navigation

- **Values that come from the loader.** `characterSet` is always `"UTF-8"`, `referrer` is `""` (in a frame: the parent's URL), and `lastModified` is the current local time. `domain` is the host of the URL and is read-only. _Elsewhere:_ WebKit takes them from the decoder and the loader. The standard gives `domain` a setter.
- **`relList.supports()`, `HTMLScriptElement.supports()`.** They answer as in WebKit: true for `preload`, `modulepreload`, `stylesheet`, `module`, `importmap` and so on. None of these does anything, and no `load` or `error` event follows. _Elsewhere:_ The same lists, and they work.
- **Images, `<style>`.** `img.complete` is true only when `src` is missing or empty, and `srcset` is not looked at. `img.decode()` rejects at once with `EncodingError`. A `<style>` has a real sheet and fires no `load`. _Elsewhere:_ The standard says `complete` is false for an unloaded image that has only `srcset`. WebKit fires `load` or `error` at a `<style>`.
- **Navigation.** Only a change of the fragment navigates, also by a click on a link: `location` changes at once, and `popstate` and then `hashchange` fire in one task. Any other navigation does nothing and says nothing, but a URL that does not parse is still a `SyntaxError`. `document.open(url, name, features)` acts as `document.open()`. _Elsewhere:_ The page is loaded, and the three-argument `open()` opens a window.
- **`history`.** `back()`, `forward()` and `go(n)` queue one task, which looks at the index when it runs. A step past either end and `go(0)` do nothing. `pushState()` and a fragment navigation cancel queued traversals, `replaceState()` does not. _Elsewhere:_ `go(0)` reloads. WebKit also limits the number of calls and the size of the state.
- **`XMLHttpRequest`: what is not checked or sent.** There is no same-origin policy: no CORS check, no preflight, no mixed content check. `withCredentials` is only stored. No cookie is sent or stored, and no `Origin` or `Referer` header is sent. `User-Agent`, `Accept-Encoding` and `Connection` are those of Bun's `fetch()`, and so are proxies from the environment. `data:`, `blob:` and `file:` URLs do what `fetch()` does with them. _Elsewhere:_ A cross-origin response without the right headers is a network error, and `file:` is refused.
- **`XMLHttpRequest`: synchronous requests.** `open(method, url, false)` works, and `send()` then throws a `NotSupportedError`. _Elsewhere:_ `send()` blocks until the response is there.
- **`XMLHttpRequest`: events.** `readystatechange` and `progress` fire once for each chunk that `fetch()` delivers, without the pause of 50 ms. There is no further `progress` at the end of the body, so an empty body gives none, and no `LOADING`, as in WebKit. The upload's `progress`, `load` and `loadend` fire together when the response's headers arrive, with everything sent. A `timeout` that is set after `send()` counts only if one was set before, as in WebKit. The timer is on the real clock under the fake timers of `bun:test`. _Elsewhere:_ Progress is reported about every 50 ms, also for the upload while it is sent. The standard fires one more `progress` at the end of every body, and lets `timeout` be set at any time.
- **`XMLHttpRequest`: the response.** The encoding of text is the byte order mark's, else the `charset`, else for XML what the XML declaration names, else UTF-8. `<meta charset>` is not looked at, and the document's `characterSet` is `"UTF-8"`. `total` is not known for a response with a `Content-Encoding`. _Elsewhere:_ `<meta charset>` is looked at, and `characterSet` is the encoding that was used.
- **`XMLHttpRequest`: methods and URLs.** A method that Bun's `fetch()` does not know is sent as `GET`, as `fetch()` does. A `blob:` URL is looked up in `send()`, not in `open()`. The class that `bun:dom` exports has no window, so its base URL is `about:blank` and a relative URL is a `SyntaxError`. It has `responseXML` and the type `document` all the same. _Elsewhere:_ Any token is a method. A worker's `XMLHttpRequest` has neither.
- **`document.cookie`.** An in-memory jar per document, which `fetch()` does not see. It honors `Expires`, `Max-Age`, `Path`, `Domain` and `Secure`, and ignores a cookie with `HttpOnly`. The default path is `/`, a string without `=` is ignored, and there is no public suffix check and no limit. _Elsewhere:_ WebKit asks the network process, and documents of one site share the jar. In RFC 6265 the default path is the directory of the URL.

### Events and tasks

- **A task that another task queues.** It runs in the same iteration of the event loop, before a timer that was set earlier and is not due yet. Both tasks run before Bun looks at its unhandled rejections, so a handler that the second task attaches is in time. _Elsewhere:_ `EventLoop::run()` takes the tasks that are queued when it starts. A task queued meanwhile is in a later batch, which is ordered with timers by time. A rejection is reported after the first task.
- **Tasks and timers.** Tasks run in the order they were queued, whatever their task source, and before a timer that is set after them. After 1,000 tasks in one iteration of the loop, the next ones wait for the next iteration, so that timers and I/O get a turn. _Elsewhere:_ Task sources have their own queues, and tasks and timers are ordered through the run loop. There is no such limit.
- **Microtasks between listeners.** Microtasks are drained after each listener of a target that belongs to a window, or of a `FileReader` or an `XMLHttpRequest`, when no script is on the stack. Bun's older event targets (`new EventTarget()`, `AbortSignal`, `MessagePort`, `WebSocket`) have no such checkpoint, as in Node. _Elsewhere:_ A checkpoint follows every listener when no script is on the stack.
- **Animation frames.** A frame is one runtime timer of 1000 / 60 ms, which keeps the process alive and which the fake timers of `bun:test` drive. All callbacks of a frame run under the timer's host function, so there is no microtask checkpoint between two callbacks. _Elsewhere:_ Frames follow the display and stop for hidden pages. A microtask checkpoint follows each callback.
- **Custom element backup queue.** One queue per document. Only the relative order of reactions for elements of two documents can differ. _Elsewhere:_ One queue per agent.
- **`Event.timeStamp`.** It is what the global object's `performance.now()` would have returned when the event was made. It is not coarsened, and under the fake timers of `bun:test` it keeps the real clock. _Elsewhere:_ WebKit uses the window's or the worker's `performance` and reduces the resolution. The web platform tests want steps of at least 5 microseconds.
- **`window.event`.** It is set on the window of the event's current target: that of a node's document or of an `XMLHttpRequest`, or the window itself. A listener on any other target (`new EventTarget()`, `AbortSignal`, `MediaQueryList`) sets none. _Elsewhere:_ It is set on the global object of the listener's realm, for every target outside a shadow tree.
- **`UIEvent.view`, `MessageEvent.source`.** They hold a `Window`, so `event.view === globalThis` is false, except in a test environment (see "A global object that stands for a window"). `{ view: globalThis }` and `{ source: globalThis }` are accepted when the global object stands for a window. While the global object stands for a window, `source` also takes any other object and gives the same object back, in the constructor and in `initMessageEvent()`, because tests written for jsdom pass a stand-in for a window. Otherwise anything but a `Window` or a `MessagePort` is a `TypeError`, as in Node. _Elsewhere:_ Both take and give the `WindowProxy`, which is the global object.
- **Inline event handlers.** The scope chain is window, document, form owner, element. The parameter is named `event` for SVG elements too. _Elsewhere:_ The window is the global object, so it is not on the scope chain. WebKit names the parameter `evt` for SVG.
- **A listener that returns a promise.** A rejection is rethrown on `process.nextTick()`, so it is an uncaught exception and not an unhandled rejection. This also holds for listeners on nodes. _Elsewhere:_ The return value is ignored.
- **A wrapper with a queued event.** The wrapper of a node, and so its listeners, stays alive while an event is queued for the node, also when the node is connected. See the line for `JSNodeCustom.cpp` under `bindings/js/`. _Elsewhere:_ WebKit asks this only for a node that is not connected. In Bun a node can be connected to a document that script no longer holds.

### Focus

- **A window always has focus.** With a window, `hasFocus()` is true, `hidden` is false and `visibilityState` is `"visible"`. Without one they are false, true and `"hidden"`. A focus change always dispatches `blur`, `focusout`, `focus` and `focusin`, and `:focus`, `:focus-visible` and `:focus-within` always match. _Elsewhere:_ WebKit asks the page. It dispatches `blur` and `focus`, and matches the three pseudo-classes, only while the page is focused.
- **Focusable elements, `autofocus`.** An element is focusable when it is connected, `supportsFocus()` holds and it is not inert. So an element with `display: none` or `hidden` can be focused, as in jsdom, and an `<area href>` like a link. `autofocus` focuses nothing by itself, but dialogs and popovers still look for their autofocus delegate. _Elsewhere:_ The element also has to be rendered, and an `<area>` needs an `<img usemap>`. Autofocus candidates are flushed when the rendering is updated.
- **`inert` and modal dialogs.** An element is inert if it or an ancestor in the composed tree has the `inert` attribute, or if it is outside an open modal dialog. This only makes it not focusable, and an element that becomes inert while it has focus is not blurred. _Elsewhere:_ The same rules, kept as an inherited bit of the style. WebKit blurs at the next style update, and `inert` also affects selection, `find()` and `innerText`.

### Forms

- **Form submission.** `requestSubmit()`, a click on a submit button and implicit submission validate, fire `submit`, build the entry list and fire `formdata`. Then nothing happens. A connected form in a document without a window does the same. _Elsewhere:_ WebKit then navigates. It returns at once when the document has no frame.
- **`submit` and `reset` from inside a form.** A `submit` or `reset` event that script dispatches at a control bubbles through the form like any other event, as the standard says and as in jsdom. Tests count on it: Testing Library's `fireEvent.submit(button)` reaches React's `onSubmit`. _Elsewhere:_ WebKit, Chromium and Firefox stop these two events at the form when they come from a descendant.
- **A `formdata` listener that disconnects the form.** The form can be submitted again later. _Elsewhere:_ WebKit leaves its "submitting" flag set, so later submissions that are not `form.submit()` do nothing.
- **Selection in text controls.** Offsets refer to `value`, and the initial state is 0, 0, `"none"`. `focus()` does not touch the selection, as the standard says. _Elsewhere:_ On focus WebKit selects all the text of a field that never had a selection, and puts a textarea's caret at 0.
- **Answers that depend on the platform upstream.** The same everywhere: the input types `color`, `date`, `datetime-local`, `month`, `time` and `week` exist, `validationMessage` is Safari's English text, `accessKeyLabel` is `"Alt+"` and the key, and a `selectionDirection` of `"none"` stays `"none"`. Every focusable control is mouse focusable, so a click on a `<label>` focuses its control. _Elsewhere:_ Safari on macOS treats `type=week` as text, gives key symbols and does not focus buttons or checkboxes on click. WebKit localizes the messages, and turns `"none"` into `"forward"` on Windows and Unix.
- **`<input type=color>`, `showPicker()`.** `#rrggbb` is lower-cased, anything else becomes `#000000`, and `alpha` and `colorSpace` change nothing. `input.showPicker()` throws `InvalidStateError` when the input is not mutable, otherwise `NotAllowedError`. `select.showPicker()` does not exist. _Elsewhere:_ WebKit and the current standard parse any CSS color. WebKit's `showPicker()` returns silently without a frame.
- **`Blob` in place of `File`.** The entry for a file input without files is one empty `Blob` without a type. `ElementInternals.setFormValue()` takes any `Blob`, and drops the `state` argument. _Elsewhere:_ The standard wants an empty `File` of the type `application/octet-stream`. `setFormValue()` takes only a `File`, a string or a `FormData`.

### Elements

- **SVG and MathML.** Eight SVG tags have an interface of their own (`svg`, `g`, `defs`, `desc`, `metadata`, `switch`, `symbol`, `title`), every other element in the SVG namespace is a plain `SVGElement`, and a MathML element is a plain `Element`. That is jsdom's list, and so are the members: `className`, `viewBox`, `preserveAspectRatio`, `requiredExtensions`, `systemLanguage`, `createSVGNumber()`, `createSVGRect()`, `getElementById()` and the four methods about redrawing. `getBBox()`, `getCTM()`, `transform`, `width`, `createSVGPoint()` and the like do not exist. `animVal` always equals `baseVal`. An SVG `<a href>` does not match `:link`, and `document.title` knows the HTML `<title>` only. _Elsewhere:_ There is an interface per SVG tag, and `MathMLElement` exists.
- **Media elements.** `play()`, `pause()`, `load()` and `addTextTrack()` do nothing and return undefined. That is deliberate: a rejected promise would be an unhandled rejection, and a pending one would hang `await`. `volumechange` and `ratechange` are dispatched synchronously from the setters. _Elsewhere:_ `play()` returns a promise and `addTextTrack()` a `TextTrack`. The two events are queued as tasks.
- **Stubs.** `canvas.getContext()` and `toDataURL()` return `null`, and `toBlob()` never calls back. A `ResizeObserver` checks its arguments and never calls its callback. `setPointerCapture()` and `releasePointerCapture()` do nothing and never throw. _Elsewhere:_ A context, a data URL and a blob. The first observation of a box that is not 0 by 0 is reported. An unknown pointer id throws `NotFoundError`.
- **`scrollTop`, `scrollLeft`.** They remember what script assigns, as integers, and `scrollTo()`, `scroll()` and `scrollBy()` write them. They are not clamped, no `scroll` event fires, and they survive removal from the document. _Elsewhere:_ The value is clamped to the scrollable area, and a `scroll` event fires.
- **`innerText`, `outerText`.** The getters return `textContent` with `<br>` as `"\n"`, also for content that CSS hides. _Elsewhere:_ That is WebKit's answer for an element that is not rendered. For a rendered one the text follows CSS and layout.
- **`isContentEditable`.** The answer comes from the nearest `contenteditable` attribute, then from `designMode`. CSS has no effect, and a document without a window answers like any other. _Elsewhere:_ WebKit reads the computed style, and always says read-only in a document that can never render.
- **Popovers and dialogs.** No close request exists: no key event and no pointer event outside closes a dialog or a popover, also with `closedby="any"`. The methods, invoker buttons and the `cancel` and `close` events work. _Elsewhere:_ A trusted Escape key or an outside click closes them. An event that script dispatches closes nothing in a browser either.
- **`<style>` text.** Assigning a `Text` node's own data to it (`text.data = text.data`) inside a `<style>` leaves the sheet as it is, with its CSSOM edits. _Elsewhere:_ WebKit takes the slow path for a `<style>` parent, so the sheet is made again.
- **`nonce`.** The content attribute is never hidden, also on a repeated `<html>` or `<body>` tag. On an SVG element the `nonce` property does not follow the attribute. _Elsewhere:_ The attribute reads as empty after insertion when the policy came in a header. SVG and MathML elements copy the attribute to the property as HTML elements do.
- **Adopted nodes.** A node without a wrapper that moves to a document of another global object gets its wrapper from whichever global object asks first. _Elsewhere:_ WebKit makes the wrapper in the old realm before the move.
- **`FileReader`.** It is a property of a window and an export of `bun:dom`, not a global of the runtime. The bytes come in one piece, so even a large file gives only one `progress` event, at the end. _Elsewhere:_ A global in windows and workers. The standard fires `progress` while reading.

### CSS and selectors

- **Computed values.** Values stay as specified: `1rem`, `bold`, `calc(...)`, `width: auto`, a relative `url()`, `display: inline` of a flex item. Colors become `rgb()` or `rgba()`, but system colors such as `canvastext` stay keywords. jsdom up to 26 answers the same, so `toHaveStyle("margin-top: 1rem")` keeps passing. _Elsewhere:_ Lengths become `px`, `bold` becomes `700`, `width` is the used width, URLs are absolute, flex items are blockified and system colors are resolved.
- **A `var()` that refers to nothing.** If a reference has no value and no fallback, also because of a cycle, the computed value is the declared text: `width: var(--x)` gives `"var(--x)"`, a shorthand gives its whole text, and so does a custom property whose own value has such a reference. The longhands of such a shorthand have their initial or inherited value. In a unit test the theme's style sheet is usually not loaded, and the declared text says more than an initial value nobody wrote: `toHaveStyle("color: var(--brand)")` passes, as on jsdom, which never substitutes. _Elsewhere:_ The declaration is invalid at computed-value time, so the property has its initial or inherited value, and the custom property has none.
- **What `getComputedStyle()` answers for.** An element that is not connected has values like any other. Nine pseudo-elements are known: `::before`, `::after`, `::marker`, `::first-line`, `::first-letter`, `::placeholder`, `::selection`, `::backdrop`, `::file-selector-button`. Any other `::x` gives an empty declaration, and rules for it never apply. _Elsewhere:_ For an element that is not connected every value is `""` and `length` is 0. WebKit knows more pseudo-elements.
- **Computed shorthand.** If one declaration of the shorthand wins for all its longhands, the answer is what an inline style with that declaration says: `1px solid red`. Otherwise it is put together from the computed longhands, except for `font`, `transition` and `animation`, which are `""`. _Elsewhere:_ Always put together from computed longhands: `1px solid rgb(255, 0, 0)`.
- **Media queries.** Only the media type counts: `screen`, `all` and `not print` are true, and any feature, such as `min-width`, makes a query false. `@media`, `<style media>` and `matchMedia()` share this rule. A query with a feature keeps the author's text. _Elsewhere:_ Features are evaluated, and `change` fires when the result changes. The text is normalized.
- **What the cascade leaves out.** `@container`, `@scope`, `@starting-style` and `::part()` rules are in the CSSOM and never apply, `@property` does nothing, and `revert-layer` acts like `revert`. A `<style title>` always applies. Logical and physical properties (`padding-block-start`, `padding-top`) are not mapped onto each other. _Elsewhere:_ All of them work. Alternate sheets are off, and the later declaration of a logical group wins.
- **User agent style.** It covers `display` for every tag, bold, italic, monospace, links, `body` margins and a few more, but not the margins and font sizes of headings and lists or the paddings and borders of controls and table cells. Of the presentational attributes only `hidden` and `dir` reach computed style. _Elsewhere:_ The full `html.css`, and attributes such as `align`, `bgcolor` and `width` map to style.
- **At-rules without an interface.** `@font-face`, `@keyframes`, `@import`, `@namespace`, `@property`, `@page` and `@counter-style` are plain `CSSRule` objects with the right `type` and the `cssText` as written. `@container`, `@scope` and `@starting-style` are plain `CSSGroupingRule` objects. `@layer` has its two interfaces: `name` and `nameList` are the text as written. _Elsewhere:_ Each has its own interface, with members such as `name`, `cssRules`, `style` and `href`.
- **Nested rules.** Declarations after a nested rule are hoisted into the rule's own block, and declarations directly in a nested at-rule show as a `& { }` style rule. `selectorText =` on a parent does not change what `&` means in its nested rules, and on a nested rule it is parsed as a top-level selector. _Elsewhere:_ Both kinds of declarations are `CSSNestedDeclarations` rules, and `&` follows the parent.
- **Values that keep the author's text.** `box-shadow`, `transform`, `transition`, `animation`, `mask`, `border-image`, `filter`, `clip-path`, `grid-template-columns` and others, as in jsdom, because the `style` attribute is in recorded DOM snapshots. `text-decoration`, `list-style`, `grid-row`, `grid-column` and `grid-area` keep it until one of their longhands is set again. _Elsewhere:_ They are normalized: `box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px red` becomes `red 0px 0px 0px 1px`.
- **Shorthands.** `columns`, `white-space`, `font-variant`, `border-image`, `mask`, `grid-template`, `page-break-after` and others are single properties, so `font` does not reset `font-variant`. `border` sets 13 properties, and `all` is one declaration that answers as if it were expanded. _Elsewhere:_ They expand to longhands. `border` gives 17, and `all` about 390.
- **Values and names that Bun's parser decides.** `font: caption` and `font` with `small-caps` are refused, `calc(50% + 0px)` comes back as `calc(50%)`, and `env()` is never substituted. `font-stretch` is the name and `font-width` the alias, there are no `-epub-` names, and a `font-family` name with a space is written with quotes. _Elsewhere:_ The `font` values are valid, the `calc()` is kept and `env()` is substituted. `font-width` is the name, and WebKit takes all quotes off.
- **`removeAttribute("style")` after a CSSOM write.** No attribute is left, and there is a mutation record. Chromium and Firefox do the same. _Elsewhere:_ WebKit's code leaves `style=""` and makes no record.
- **Namespaces.** `@namespace` is kept as text and does nothing. A selector with a prefix other than `*` or the empty one is invalid, also in a sheet that declares the prefix, and `*|e` is written `e`. _Elsewhere:_ WebKit resolves prefixes and the default namespace from `@namespace` rules. In `querySelector()` it rejects prefixes too.
- **Selectors whose validity differs.** Invalid in Bun: `[*]`, `[*|*]`, `:matches()`, `:-webkit-drag`, the longer `:-webkit-autofill-*` names, `::grammar-error`, `::spelling-error`, `:host(:not(a b))`. Valid in Bun: `:lang(--x)`, and `:nth-child(n-99999999999)`, whose number saturates. `::CUE(b)` is invalid too: the names of `::cue()`, `::picker()` and `::view-transition-*()` are case-sensitive. _Elsewhere:_ WebKit accepts the first list and rejects the second, and Firefox decides both as Bun does. WebKit accepts the names in any case.
- **Pseudo-classes after a pseudo-element.** `:is()`, `:where()` and `:not()` after a pseudo-element are invalid: `a::before:not(b)`. After `::part()` they are valid only if their content may follow `::part()`. The scrollbar pseudo-classes (`:horizontal`, `:start`, `:window-inactive` and the like) are valid only after a `::-webkit-scrollbar` pseudo-element. _Elsewhere:_ WebKit accepts all of these, and the scrollbar ones anywhere. Chromium and Firefox reject the logical ones too.
- **Valid, but never match.** The pseudo-classes for fullscreen, picture-in-picture, media playback (`:playing`, `:paused`, `:muted` and the like), text tracks (`:past`, `:future`), autofill and view transitions. `:modal` matches only a `<dialog>`, and `:open` only a `<dialog>` or a `<details>`. _Elsewhere:_ WebKit matches them. `:modal` also matches a fullscreen element, and `:open` a control whose picker is open.
- **`:hover`, `:active`.** `:hover` never matches, because nothing calls `setHovered()`, and dispatched mouse events change neither state. `:active` is set only by upstream's simulated clicks and key handling. Entering or leaving the top layer moves `:focus-within` across the boundary, but not these two. _Elsewhere:_ WebKit sets both from real pointer input. All three stop at a top layer boundary.
- **Matching where Bun follows the standard.** `[TYPE=a]` and `[|type=a]` compare the value case-insensitively for an HTML element in an HTML document, as `[type=a]` does. With `:nth-last-child(An+B of S)` an element that does not match S never matches. _Elsewhere:_ WebKit looks up the name as written and treats the empty prefix as a prefix, so both compare case-sensitively. There such an element can match if its parent is a `DocumentFragment`, a `ShadowRoot` or the `Document`.
- **Forgiven members of `:is()` and `:where()`.** `selectorText` leaves out a forgiven member that Bun's grammar cannot hold: `:is(::before, .a)` prints as `:is(.a)`. An unknown pseudo-class is printed: `:is(:nonsense, #a)`. _Elsewhere:_ WebKit prints every forgiven member as written.

### Window

- **Making a window.** `new Window({ url })` makes an ordinary object. `url` is the only option, has to be an absolute URL (else `TypeError`), defaults to `about:blank`, and nothing is fetched from it. The document is always `<!DOCTYPE html><html><head></head><body></body></html>`, the size is 1024 by 768 with a `devicePixelRatio` of 1, and `isSecureContext` is true. _Elsewhere:_ The window is the global object of a realm, and a navigation fills its document.
- **Realms and constructors.** All windows of a global object share one realm and one set of prototypes. `Comment`, `Text`, `DocumentFragment`, `Document`, `Range`, `DOMParser`, `XMLHttpRequest`, `HTMLElement`, `Image`, `Audio` and `Option` need a document, so each window has its own copy, with a shared `prototype`. `X.prototype.constructor` is the global object's copy, which has no window: `new (node.constructor)()` throws a `ReferenceError`. _Elsewhere:_ Each window is a realm with its own prototypes, and `window.X === X.prototype.constructor`.
- **Runtime classes on a window.** `Event`, `EventTarget`, `AbortController`, `DOMException`, `FormData`, `Blob`, `File`, `URL`, `fetch`, the timers and the like are Bun's own, and differ from the standard as they do without a DOM. `new Blob(["x"], { type: "text/plain" }).type` has `;charset=utf-8`, `new FormData(x)` ignores an `x` that is not a `<form>`, `new ErrorEvent("error").error` is `null`, and `fetch("/x")` does not resolve against `location`. _Elsewhere:_ WebKit's own classes. The answers are `"text/plain"`, a `TypeError` and `undefined`.
- **Names a window does not have.** A name that nothing on the prototype chain has is read from the realm's global object: `window.Array`, `window.setTimeout`, `window.process`. No list of keys shows these names, and a write makes an own property of the window only. So `vm.createContext(window)` gets the outer realm's `Array`, `Object`, `Function` and `eval` unless the window has its own. _Elsewhere:_ The window is the global object.
- **Elements by `id` or `name`.** They come last, after the global object: `<div id="process">` is not `window.process`. An `id` that is an array index is not found. `document[name]` for an `<iframe>` is the element. _Elsewhere:_ Named elements come right after the prototype chain, and `document[name]` gives the frame's window.
- **Where the members live.** Attributes are configurable accessors on `Window.prototype`, and a window's prototype can be set. Operations are there too, and each window has a bound own copy, so `const { getComputedStyle } = window` works. `alert`, `confirm`, `prompt`, `print`, `scrollTo` and the like do nothing and return undefined, so Bun's own `alert`, `confirm` and `prompt`, which read stdin, are never reached. _Elsewhere:_ All members of a global are own properties of the window, and its prototype is immutable.
- **A global object that stands for a window.** After `setGlobalObjectWindow(window)` the caller's `globalThis` is accepted where an argument or a dictionary member has to be a `Window`, but not as `this`. It also decides the sender of `postMessage()`. After `setGlobalObjectWindow(window, true)`, which `bun test --environment=bun:dom` calls, it also goes the other way: where native code hands that window to script (`event.view`, `event.source`, `event.target`, `this` in a listener, `defaultView`, a frame's `parent` and `top`, `opener`), script gets `globalThis`. `frames` is the exception and gives the `Window` object, because `globalThis[0]` does not find a frame and `frames[0]` has to. Only Bun's own JavaScript and `bun:internal-for-testing` reach the function. _Elsewhere:_ The global object is the window.
- **`postMessage()`.** The sender (`event.source`, `event.origin`, the meaning of `"/"`) is the window the caller's global object stands for, or else the target itself. A target origin other than the window's drops the message silently. A window with an opaque origin only takes `"*"`, and `"/"` from itself. _Elsewhere:_ The sender is the incumbent global object.
- **`navigator`.** Each window has its own, of the class `window.Navigator`, with the members of jsdom's. `userAgent` (`"Bun/..."`), `platform`, `hardwareConcurrency`, `language` and `languages` are the runtime's, and `onLine` is `true`. `appCodeName`, `appName`, `appVersion`, `product`, `productSub`, `vendor`, `vendorSub`, `cookieEnabled` and `javaEnabled()` answer as in jsdom, and `plugins` and `mimeTypes` are empty. The runtime's `navigator` and its global `Navigator` are another class, with only the first five, as in Node: old copies of jsbn read `window.crypto` where `appName` is `"Netscape"`. `Plugin`, `MimeType`, `clipboard`, `locks`, `sendBeacon()` and the rest do not exist. _Elsewhere:_ One `Navigator` class per realm, with many more members.
- **Properties of `location`.** Its members are own and enumerable, but configurable and writable, so `location.assign = mock` and `spyOn(location, "assign")` work. `window.location` is a configurable accessor on `Window.prototype`, and `Object.preventExtensions(location)` works. _Elsewhere:_ `[LegacyUnforgeable]`: own and not configurable, also on the window. `preventExtensions` fails.
- **`localStorage`, `sessionStorage`.** In memory, one of each per window, also for a frame's window and its parent, so no `storage` event fires by itself. The quota is 5,000,000 UTF-16 code units for keys and values together, and `key(n)` and `Object.keys()` are in insertion order. An opaque origin throws `SecurityError` from the getter: `about:blank`, `data:`, and also `file:`. _Elsewhere:_ Shared by the documents of an origin, and kept on disk. WebKit's `StorageMap` is a hash map, so the order is not defined.
- **`Selection`.** `toString()` is the range's, so it does not look at `user-select` or `display`. `selectionchange` goes to the document as one task for all changes made before it runs. It does not fire when script moves the selection's range or the tree changes under it, and a range that is moved out of the document stays the selection's. _Elsewhere:_ `toString()` follows rendering. The event fires for those changes too.
- **`close()`.** `closed` becomes true. The listeners of the window and the document go, and queued traversals, animation frames and tasks do nothing. Its `XMLHttpRequest`s that are under way are cancelled without an event and are `UNSENT` again, `open()` throws an `InvalidStateError` from then on, and `send()` is a network error. The document stays. The windows of its frames are closed and taken from their frame elements, and the windows it has opened are closed. _Elsewhere:_ `close()` is ignored on a window that no script opened, and closing a window leaves the ones it opened alone.
- **Lifetime.** A window is collected like any object. Its `location`, `history`, `screen`, storage areas, selection and nodes keep it alive, and so does a queued task, a pending frame or an `XMLHttpRequest`. A window and the windows of its connected frames keep each other alive, and an opened window keeps its opener. An event does not keep the wrapper of its `view`, nor the selection that of its range: after a collection `event.view` and `getRangeAt(0)` can give a new wrapper without the expando properties. _Elsewhere:_ The window lives as long as its realm. The frame keeps the `WindowProxy` alive, and the range's wrapper is reachable from the window.
- **Frames.** A connected `<iframe>` or `<frame>` in a document with a window has a window of its own, made during the insertion. Every insertion and every change of `src` or `srcdoc` makes a new window and closes the old one. A removed frame's window is closed, and its `parent`, `top` and `frameElement` are null. `about:blank`, no `src`, a `src` that does not parse and `javascript:` (never run, and the document has the parent's URL) give `<html><head></head><body></body></html>`. `srcdoc` is parsed during the insertion, and its scripts are not run. Any other `src` gives an empty document with that URL that stays at `"loading"` and fires nothing, also for another origin. `<object>` and `<embed>` have no frame. _Elsewhere:_ A navigation keeps the `WindowProxy` and replaces the document later, in a task. `contentDocument` is null for another origin.
- **`load` at a frame element.** The timing is jsdom's. A frame element that has no listener of any kind when it is inserted is told during the insertion, and its window hears `load` once more in a microtask. Any other is told in a microtask: until then `readyState` is `"loading"`, and then `readystatechange`, `DOMContentLoaded`, `readystatechange`, `load` at the window and `load` at the element follow at once. _Elsewhere:_ WebKit and Chrome always fire `load` for `about:blank` during the insertion, and none at the window. `srcdoc` loads in a task.
- **`window[0]`, `window.length`, `window[name]`.** The frames of the document tree in tree order, worked out on each access. A frame in a shadow tree has a window and is not among them. An indexed property that script has defined on the window comes first. `window[name]` goes by the `name` attribute as it is now. _Elsewhere:_ WebKit goes by the order in which the frames were made. Script cannot define an indexed property on a window. The name is the one the frame was made with, or `window.name`.
- **`window.open()`.** Always a new window at `about:blank` with `<html><head></head><body></body></html>`, the opener's origin and base URL, and `opener` set. The URL is only checked (`SyntaxError`). `_self`, `_parent` and `_top` give those windows, any other name becomes `window.name` and never finds an existing window, and `noopener` or `noreferrer` gives null. All other features are ignored, and features are only split at commas. _Elsewhere:_ The URL is loaded, and a name that is in use gives that window.

### Interfaces and members that are missing

- **Trusted types.** `TrustedHTML`, `TrustedScript`, `TrustedScriptURL` and `trustedTypes` do not exist. Members such as `innerHTML` take any value as a string. _Elsewhere:_ WebKit has them and enforces them when a content security policy asks for it.
- **`DataTransfer`, `TextEvent`.** Undefined on purpose: testing libraries use their own `DataTransfer` stub only then, and with `"TextEvent" in window` React DOM feeds `onBeforeInput` from `textInput`, which nothing dispatches. `ClipboardEvent.clipboardData` and `DragEvent.dataTransfer` take any value, such as `{ files: [] }`. `InputEvent.dataTransfer` does not exist, and `document.createEvent("TextEvent")` still makes a `TextEvent`. _Elsewhere:_ WebKit exposes both. The attributes are `DataTransfer?`, and a plain object throws a `TypeError`.
- **`TouchEvent`.** `touches`, `targetTouches` and `changedTouches` are plain arrays. The constructor makes each from anything that can be iterated and keeps the items as they are, plain objects too. `ontouchstart`, `ontouchmove`, `ontouchend` and `ontouchcancel` exist on windows, documents and elements on every platform, so `"ontouchstart" in window` is true. All of this is what jsdom does. _Elsewhere:_ The lists are `TouchList`s of `Touch` objects, and anything else is a `TypeError`. WebKit has touch events only on touch platforms.
- **Interfaces that a window lacks.** `CloseWatcher`, `DOMPoint`, `DOMPointReadOnly`, `DOMQuad`, `DOMMatrix`, `IntersectionObserver`, XPath, XSLT, `Touch`, `TouchList`, `MutationEvent`, `DeviceMotionEvent`, `DeviceOrientationEvent`, `GamepadEvent`, `BlobEvent`, `MediaQueryListEvent` and `FileReaderSync` are undefined. _Elsewhere:_ WebKit exposes all but `MutationEvent`, and touch events only on touch platforms.
- **`checkVisibility()`, `adoptedStyleSheets`.** Left out on purpose. Without a renderer `checkVisibility()` would always say false, so libraries that test for it would think everything is hidden. Without `adoptedStyleSheets`, feature detection in Lit and others takes `<style>`, as on jsdom. `new CSSStyleSheet()` and `replaceSync()` work, but the sheet cannot be attached to anything. _Elsewhere:_ WebKit has both.
- **Other members that are missing.** `execCommand()`, `evaluate()` and the rest of XPath, `caretRangeFromPoint()`, `elementFromPoint()`, `elementsFromPoint()`, `Range.expand()`, `requestIdleCallback()`, `visualViewport`, `history.scrollRestoration`, `location.ancestorOrigins`. Of `Selection`: `modify()`, `getComposedRanges()`, `baseNode`, `extentNode`. Of the CSSOM: `CSSStyleSheet.replace()`, `insertRule()` on a style rule, `getPropertyCSSValue()`, and all of `CSS` but `escape()` and `supports()`. _Elsewhere:_ WebKit has them.
- **Features that a setting decides upstream.** Off: reference target, scoped custom element registries (`new CustomElementRegistry()` throws a `TypeError`), `moveBefore()` and `connectedMoveCallback`, `Observable`, mutation events, the `switch` control, the class prefix selector `.a-*`, `:optimum` and its two relatives. On: `PointerEvent.altitudeAngle` and `azimuthAngle`, and `getCoalescedEvents()` without a secure context. _Elsewhere:_ The first group is off by default in WebKit too, or on only for Cocoa, and WebKit's test runner turns it on. The angles are on by default only on Cocoa.

### Errors

- **An exception from a listener or an animation frame callback.** When the current target belongs to a window, a cancelable `error` event fires at that window. If nobody cancels it, `window.console.error(exception)` is called, and there is no uncaught exception. `filename`, `lineno` and `colno` come from the top frame of the stack and are not source-mapped. _Elsewhere:_ The standard reports to the global object of the listener's realm.
- **Other exceptions.** A target without a window (a plain `EventTarget`, `AbortSignal`, `WebSocket`, a node of a `DOMParser` document) keeps Bun's uncaught exception. So do mutation observers, custom element reactions, timers and `reportError()`. No `unhandledrejection` fires at a window. _Elsewhere:_ All of them are reported at the window.
- **Dispatching an event that is being dispatched.** A node throws an `InvalidStateError` `DOMException`. Every other target, a `Window` too, throws Node's `ERR_EVENT_RECURSION`. _Elsewhere:_ Always `InvalidStateError`.
- **Kinds of errors.** A `TypeError` for a wrong or missing argument, a missing dictionary member, a wrong `this` or an illegal constructor has Node's `code` property, for example `ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE`. The DOM throws a `DOMException` named `"SyntaxError"`, while `WebSocket`, `crypto.subtle` and `performance.measure()` keep throwing a JavaScript `SyntaxError`. _Elsewhere:_ A plain `TypeError`, and a `DOMException` everywhere.
- **Errors that WebKit does not throw.** `new HTMLOutputElement()` throws, as in the standard. `CustomStateSet.forEach()` with a callback that is not callable throws at once, also on an empty set. _Elsewhere:_ WebKit's IDL makes the element constructable. WebKit throws for the callback only when the set has an entry.
